stories.Headline: David Tepper sells Broadcom and AMD stakes to buy Nvidia and Micron shares
stories.Summary:
Billionaire David Tepper of Appaloosa Management reshuffled his artificial intelligence semiconductor positions during the third quarter. The owner of the Carolina Panthers exited his positions in Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices. He used this rotation to buy shares of Micron and Nvidia. Tepper also reduced his stake in Alphabet by nearly half. These moves occurred as he managed his estimated net worth of 28.5 billion dollars.

The rotation involves selling Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices to buy Nvidia and Micron. Tepper cut his Alphabet stake nearly in half during the third quarter of 2026. He bought Nvidia shares before Jensen Huang stepped down as the company chief executive. Alphabet co-developed Tensor Processing Units with Broadcom to deliver better performance per dollar. These TPUs are used in Alphabet's new TPU 8tx AI system.

Geoffrey Seiler from The Motley Fool believes Tepper made a mistake with these specific trades. Seiler prefers the three stocks Tepper sold over the shares of Nvidia. He argues that Nvidia could face margin compression and a loss of market share. Seiler notes that memory tends to be a commodity with big boom and bust cycles. He warns that Micron is highly exposed to changes in conventional memory prices.

Counterpoint Research projects that custom AI chip shipments will surpass data center GPU shipments in 2028. Bloomberg Intelligence believes TPU sales outside Google Cloud could grow to 135 billion dollars by 2028. Anthropic revealed that its Claude Mythos model can run on AMD GPUs in two to three days. This development affects Nvidia by narrowing its CUDA moat and opening doors for ASICs. Large customers, except Space Exploration Technologies, are developing their own custom chips.

Alphabet developed its TPUs more than a decade ago to create a comprehensive ecosystem. Anthropic is now using these solutions, as is the company known as OpenAI. Advanced Micro Devices recently started shipping Helios systems that combine GPUs, CPUs, and networking. These systems are significantly cheaper than the end to end server racks sold by Nvidia. GF Securities expects the NAND flash memory market to become oversupplied as soon as next year.

Nvidia may face lower profitability even if the company manages to grow its total revenue. The market is moving from the research phase into a global rollout called Act 2. It remains open whether Tepper's rotation into Nvidia and Micron will actually pay off. The articles do not state if Tepper will change his positions again soon. They leave the future performance of the Helios systems and TPU sales as projections.

This Billionaire Just Made a Bundle Off A.I. But It Could Have Been More.

stories.Headline: Sony and Warner sue Anthropic over pirated lyrics used to train Claude
stories.Summary:
Sony Music and Warner Music's publishing arms sued Anthropic in California federal court on August 28, 2026, a filing reported September 1, accusing the company of pirating song lyrics and sheet music to train its Claude AI chatbot. The suit claims Anthropic misused copyrighted song compositions, including hundreds of lyrics and sheet music from The Beatles, Taylor Swift, Michael Jackson and hundreds of other artists. The labels say Anthropic downloaded millions of pirated books from LibGen and PiLiMi, including books containing copyrighted lyrics and sheet music. The case names CEO Dario Amodei and co-founder Benjamin Mann individually. It was filed in the U.S. District Court, Northern District of California.

The labels seek damages of up to $150,000 for each infringed copyright, covering tens of thousands of compositions, and a court order barring Anthropic from using their works. Universal Music Group and Sony Music filed a second copyright lawsuit against Suno on September 18, 2026, in the U.S. District Court, District of Massachusetts, a 45-page complaint targeting Suno's v6 model. The labels claim v6, which Suno said is trained exclusively on licensed music, actually uses their recordings without consent, and that because the new models are partly built on users' outputs derived from former models, they remain in violation. Jason Isbell filed a proposed class action against Suno on August 31, 2026, with David Lowery, Guy Forsyth and Eduardo Calle, on behalf of musicians whose names Suno has accepted as prompts. SOCAN, the Society of Composers, Authors and Music Publishers of Canada, filed a statement of claim reported September 15, 2026, citing 150 Suno songs it says are identical or nearly identical to works by Joni Mitchell, The Weeknd, The Tragically Hip and others, seeking $20,000 per work and $10,000,000 total.

Universal Music Group sued DistroKid, in a filing reported September 15, 2026, accusing the distributor of flooding streaming platforms with AI-generated slop and of violating federal copyright laws and Delaware's Deceptive Trade Practices Act. Germany's Federal Court of Justice issued its Metall auf Metall VI decision on September 3, 2026, ruling the disputed use permissible under the pastiche exception for the period from June 7, 2021, when the relevant German provision came into force. The US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit heard arguments on September 25, 2026, in SoundExchange's appeal against Music Choice, and has not yet ruled. SoundExchange says SiriusXM's alleged underpayment now exceeds USD $400 million, a claim SiriusXM denies, and the complaint claimed Music Choice invented its own formula for allocating BES receipts, which the CRB's regulations do not permit. The appeal has put SoundExchange's $3.4 million lawsuit against Sonos on hold.

Music Choice has denied underpaying, arguing that under the rule it owes royalties only on revenue from music it provides exclusively to business customers. Suno is asking a federal judge to dismiss the Isbell lawsuit, arguing that using an artist's name to describe a musical style is protected speech, comparing its technology to a producer asking musicians to create something with more of a Jason Isbell vibe. District Judge Angel Kelley has not ruled on Suno's dismissal request, and the musicians are scheduled to respond by December 1, with Suno's reply due December 15. Putting Jason Isbell into Suno created a song called Paper Bell, described by the AI software as a contemporary Americana singer-songwriter track with fingerpicked acoustic guitar, featuring a male voice imitating Isbell's vocal elements. Warner broke away from the $500-million joint copyright lawsuit originally launched by Warner, Sony and Universal against Suno and has since signed a licensing deal with Suno.

Universal Music Group sued Anthropic in 2023 and earlier this year over the alleged use of copyrighted song lyrics in AI training, and Anthropic already paid $1.5 billion to resolve a class action from a group of authors. Suno launched v6, its first model trained on licensed music, weeks before the second suit, after partnering with Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe. The original label suit against Suno was filed over two years earlier. The Kraftwerk case is the legal ancestor of basically every sampling lawsuit filed in the United States since, including early cases like Bridgeport Music v. Dimension Films.

The SoundExchange dispute with Music Choice is more than seven years old, originally filed years ago. The second UMG and Sony suit against Suno is still in early stages, so no settlement talk yet. Suno has responded to each suit differently, settling with some labels while fighting others in court. SOCAN's lawsuit raises questions about the place of Canadian artists in a music industry increasingly shaped by American tech companies. The articles leave open how Judge Kelley will rule on Suno's dismissal request, how the Second Circuit will decide the SoundExchange appeal, and how the Anthropic, DistroKid and SOCAN cases will proceed.

stories.Headline: SAP CFO Dominik Asam reports a 70 basis point fall in cloud gross margin
stories.Summary:
SAP shares closed Friday at €181.10, down 2.1%, as a wave of selling in AI and technology names rolled from Wall Street and Asia into European markets. The retreat came even as Anthropic made its market debut, an event that, according to Reuters, failed to restore investor confidence in the AI sector. Questions over whether hefty AI spending will eventually translate into durable returns continued to hang over software stocks. The selling pressure hit SAP alongside other technology names despite the company's own AI announcements during the week.

Speaking Thursday at Morgan Stanley's technology conference, CFO Dominik Asam said SAP's cloud gross margin fell 70 basis points year on year on a currency-adjusted basis. He pointed to the product mix and introductory offers for AI products as contributing factors, Reuters reported. The disclosure landed as a reminder that SAP's AI build-out carries a near-term cost. To give investors a clearer read on that business, Asam said SAP will introduce a new metric in January covering revenue from its Business AI Platform. The gauge targets a specifically defined slice of SAP's AI operations, while his margin commentary addressed the cloud segment as a whole.

On the corporate front, SAP has completed its acquisition of TechWolf, a provider of an AI platform for work intelligence. SAP expects the business to become the intelligent core of its SuccessFactors portfolio, supporting AI-driven personnel and workforce planning. The company's retail ambitions were on display as well: on 11 November, SAP and VF Corporation opened the S.Fashion innovation space at SAP headquarters in Walldorf, where the partners will test AI-powered processes for the fashion trade, including a smart fashion store. These moves extend SAP's AI reach into workforce planning and retail processes beyond its core software business.

Separately, board member and Chief Customer Officer Thomas Saueressig has announced he will leave to take a role outside the company. He will remain in his post until the end of March 2027, with Emmanuel Raptopoulos set to take over his duties on an interim basis from January. IONOS has appointed Saueressig as its CEO effective 1 April 2027, and Achim Weiß will step down from that role on 31 March 2027. The articles do not say what happens next beyond these dates and appointments.

stories.Headline: Karnataka governor Sudha Yadav calls deepfakes and online harassment threats to women's safety and leadership
stories.Summary:
Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav said on Wednesday that deepfakes created using artificial intelligence and online harassment are emerging as serious threats to women's safety and their participation in public life, according to a statement. She called for stronger legal safeguards, greater accountability from social media platforms and effective measures to strengthen women's digital security and leadership. Women should not remain merely users of digital technology but should emerge as leaders, innovators and decision-makers, which she said requires a safe digital environment, strong legal protection and effective mentoring mechanisms. She expressed concern over the circulation of misinformation and the harassment of women on social media, saying such technologies are being misused particularly to silence women in public life and undermine public confidence in their leadership. Yadav was speaking at the valedictory function of the two-day inaugural Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians India Region Conference at Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru.

She stressed the need to improve digital literacy among women, particularly those from rural areas and disadvantaged communities, and suggested establishing mentoring mechanisms through which experienced women representatives could guide newly elected members. She said democracy could become truly inclusive and representative only when women participated safely and actively, and expressed hope that the deliberations at the conference would translate into effective policy decisions. Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh Narayan Singh, addressing the function, said protecting women's privacy and dignity in the digital world, alongside strengthening their political participation, was one of the major challenges today. He said misuse of social media, cyber harassment, deepfakes and AI-based attacks were seriously affecting the public lives of women representatives, and stressed the need to enhance legal awareness, ensure effective enforcement and increase public awareness. He recalled India's democratic traditions, referring to the ideals of collective deliberation and consensus-building in the Rig Veda and the 12th-century Anubhava Mantapa in Karnataka as outstanding examples of democratic values, and he recalled the contributions of women leaders including Rani Lakshmibai, Begum Hazrat Mahal, Sarojini Naidu, Aruna Asaf Ali, Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay and Durgabai Deshmukh to the freedom struggle and nation-building.

Harivansh said the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, also known as the Women's Reservation Act, was a significant step towards expanding women's representation and leadership in Indian democracy, and that it would enable women to shoulder greater responsibilities from local bodies to state legislatures and Parliament. He said 25 speakers had presented their views in various sessions during the two-day conference, including 17 on the first day, and that MPs, legislators from different states and subject experts took part in deliberations he described as fruitful. CWP India Region Chairperson D Purandeswari said the conference had been successful, with the active participation of more than 150 delegates from different states and Union Territories. She said digital empowerment and digital safety of women cannot be treated as separate issues, and that while technology had opened up new opportunities in governance and public engagement, the absence of a safe environment was hindering women's equal participation.

She said cyberstalking, coordinated trolling, online harassment, misuse of personal information and the growing incidence of deepfakes were threatening not only the reputation of women leaders but also public confidence in democracy, and that governments, legislatures, police departments, technology companies and civil society needed to work together to address these challenges. Purandeswari said that alongside increasing women's representation numerically, their capabilities and influence in decision-making also needed to be strengthened, and she called for formal and informal mentoring mechanisms for first-time women representatives to help them discharge their responsibilities effectively. Delivering the valedictory address, Karnataka Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed said women's empowerment was not merely about increasing their numbers in legislatures but also about strengthening their voice, influence and leadership in decision-making. He said the real success of the conference would not be measured by the speeches or discussions held there but by the actions taken in the days ahead, and that a safe digital environment for women, effective mentoring for emerging women leaders and greater influence for women in democratic institutions should be their commitments.

stories.Headline: Jensen and Lori Huang move 59 million Nvidia shares into a family trust before affair allegations and a stock plunge
stories.Summary:
Former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and his wife Lori Huang transferred stock into a family trust in March. This move occurred months before allegations of an extramarital affair surfaced and company shares tumbled. The couple moved 59 million Nvidia shares into the Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust. These shares were transferred as two grantor-retained annuity trusts reached the end of their terms. The total holding was valued at a minimum of 10.5 billion dollars at that time.

The couple set up two grantor-retained annuity trusts in March 2016 with 51 million dollars in stock. They created four trusts in total, including two with four-year terms and two with ten-year terms. The value of shares held through trusts set up in 2016 rose 22,161 percent over the decade. These filings were cited by a U.S. weekly business magazine on November 22. The couple lives in California, which is a community property state.

The articles do not provide specific statements from Jensen Huang or Lori Huang regarding the transfer. Wealth management specialists told Barron's that this was one of the most remarkable wealth transfers they had seen. The board of Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as the interim chief executive. Huang stepped down on the 12th as multiple allegations of extramarital affairs emerged. He remains the largest shareholder with a stake of about 3.5 percent.

Market observers noted that the transfer took place just months before the stock collapsed amid affair allegations. They stated that the structure is difficult for ordinary people to use and could draw ethical scrutiny. Shareholders were affected as Nvidia shares fell more than 14 percent on the 20th alone. The stock has dropped more than 30 percent since the affair allegations first surfaced. Bloomberg reported that market capitalization fell below 4 trillion dollars for the first time since last July.

The couple funded the initial trusts a month after the February earnings call in 2016. During that call, Huang highlighted the artificial intelligence potential of chips used mainly for video games. Huang co-founded the company in 1993 and held a stake worth 130 billion to 150 billion dollars. The New York Times provided the figures regarding his current shareholding value. The articles describe grantor-retained annuity trusts as estate-planning vehicles used by some wealthy Americans.

Forbes reported that Lori Huang could receive nearly half of a net worth of 155.2 billion dollars if divorced. The articles leave open whether the couple will actually divorce or if legal disputes will arise. It remains unclear if the ethical scrutiny mentioned by observers will lead to formal investigations. The text does not state if the interim chief executive will become the permanent leader. No further details are provided regarding the specific nature of the affair allegations.

stories.Headline: Nvidia and IBM launch joint research to correct quantum errors using GPUs and AI
stories.Summary:
Nvidia and IBM, joined by the U.S. Department of Energy's Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory, announced they will launch full-scale joint research to correct quantum computer calculation errors using GPUs and AI. The two companies disclosed the research plan to coincide with SC26, an international supercomputing conference held in Chicago. In the joint research, a quantum computer equipped with IBM's Nighthawk quantum processor and Nvidia's AI computing system DGX B200 will be placed side by side in the same facility and linked to each other. Nvidia also unveiled TCBP-JOBS, an algorithm for quantum error correction research. A research team from IBM, the Institute of Physical and Chemical Research, and Nvidia combined a quantum computer with GPUs to calculate the molecular structure of iron and sulfur contained in proteins and other substances in living organisms.

In the company's tests, error decoding speed improved by up to 13,000x compared with major existing methods, and the time required to study the design of a new quantum computer can be shortened from 12 weeks to 45 minutes. According to IBM, calculation accuracy improved 79-fold compared with conventional experiments of the same kind. In separate research, the binding structure of a drug-discovery-related protein and a candidate compound was modeled at a scale of up to 12,635 atoms, and the work was selected as a finalist for the 2026 ACM Gordon Bell Prize. The two companies will also advance efforts to connect quantum processors to Slurm, the open-source software widely used for supercomputer job management. Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory will leverage knowledge cultivated in high-energy and nuclear physics research to participate in error correction and the design of next-generation computers.

Krista Svore, Nvidia's vice president of quantum computing application research, said that to make quantum computers useful for science, progress is needed in everything, including error correction, application fields, and the systems that connect quantum processors with high-speed computing. Ian Buck, Nvidia's vice president, noted that scientific simulation requires CPUs that can maintain performance while continuously moving large amounts of data, explaining that Vera eliminates the bottleneck between computation and data transfer. The company said this is performance in a specific error-correction task and does not mean the quantum computer itself became 13,000x faster at computation. The company stated that all figures are test results under specific conditions announced by each company and do not guarantee the performance of the products as a whole. The articles state that the timing for general-purpose quantum computers to reach practical use remains unclear.

Terray Therapeutics further trained the model to extract chemical reaction information from scientific figures and diagrams, identifying about 76% of the reactions described in test data. Biotech company Therna applied the model to the design of messenger RNA medicines, and the accuracy of predicting the range of protein expression levels reportedly nearly doubled compared with existing state-of-the-art models. The U.S. Argonne National Laboratory is incorporating Nemotron into multiple AI agents that design and evaluate protein candidates for treating cancer and other diseases. The German Climate Computing Center will adopt Vera for its next-generation supercomputer HLRE-5, targeted to begin operation in early 2028. Vera-equipped racks are scheduled to ship from early 2027 through Dell, HPE, Lenovo, and Supermicro.

Quantum computers use qubits, basic units that can handle 0 and 1 simultaneously, and hold the potential to solve problems that conventional machines cannot solve in realistic time. However, errors arise easily from slight changes in the external environment, making quantum error correction, distributing information across multiple physical qubits to detect and fix errors, indispensable. This correction computation is enormous, and high-speed processing via GPUs is key. According to estimates published by the International Energy Agency on November 19, 2026, data centers worldwide consumed just under 500 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025, accounting for 1.7% of global power demand. If current policies continue, data center power demand is projected to roughly double 2025 levels by 2030.

Nvidia simultaneously announced a suite of AI models for scientific researchers, Nemotron for Science, and the foundation for its high-performance computing CPU Vera. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL was combined with chemical data and additional training methods, enabling it to read chemical reactions described in papers and draft experimental procedures, as well as support the design of proteins and drug candidate substances. A dataset containing about 50,000 questions for evaluating and training chemical reasoning, LitmusBench v0.2, was also released, and the models and data are available on Hugging Face. The company unveiled a Vera rack system equipped with 192 of its own designed CPUs, featuring about 300 terabytes of memory and 1 petabyte of storage, with 88 cores and 176 threads per CPU, memory bandwidth of 1.2 terabytes per second, and more than 200 terabytes per second across the entire system. In the company's tests, fluid simulation performance was 1.9x that of x86-based systems and 2.4x in performance per watt, and for weather forecasting models it expects 1.6x performance and 2x energy efficiency.

stories.Headline: South Korea's president orders a full overhaul of national exams after 111 CSAT cheating cases
stories.Summary:
The 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test was held on the morning of the 19th, and test-takers at Gwangnam High School in Gwangjin-gu, Seoul, made their final preparations. The CSAT was held amid concerns over AI-enabled cheating, and it has now finished. A perfect scorer on the Legal Education Eligibility Test died on CSAT day. The exam cheating scandal is expected to persist in Korean society. Immediate tasks include responses to cheating in the university admissions process following the CSAT.

According to Kyunghyang Shinmun reporting on the 20th, the CSAT concluded the previous day and university entrance tests are set to begin in earnest this weekend. Fourteen universities, including Korea University, Kyung Hee University, Sungkyunkwan University, and Sogang University, are administering early-admission essay tests on the 21st and 22nd. Korea University has prepared internal AI-related guidelines, banning possession of all electronic devices and strengthening inspections of test-takers' belongings. Kyung Hee University will hand out disposable aprons to candidates to block devices such as micro-cameras. Checks using electronic detectors will also be strengthened when candidates use the restroom during the test.

Prime Minister Han Seong-suk held the first meeting of the pan-government CSAT Cheating Response Task Force. He announced that cheating not detected in test rooms would be pursued to the end and met with a zero-tolerance approach. According to the government, as of the day in question, 111 test-takers had been caught cheating. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said two cases are under investigation at local police stations, one in which a mobile phone was hidden in a shoe insole and another in which a phone was concealed in clothing and brought in. The prime minister has also issued a special directive to the Ministry of Education to maintain the storage status of the CSAT test papers from last year.

The Ministry of Employment and Labor and the Human Resources Development Service of Korea will conduct a full-scale review for cheating across the 528 national qualification exam sites administered this year. They plan to identify suspicious cases such as scores markedly higher than the three-year average or unusually large gaps between ranked score groups among candidates, review the answer sheets, and then refer cases for investigation. Allegations of AI-enabled cheating by the top scorer on the certified tax accountant exam this year and allegations of LEET cheating by the LEET perfect scorer are under police investigation. The police plan to continue the investigation despite the death of the LEET perfect scorer and to look into allegations that he cheated on the CSAT last year. Not only the CSAT this year but also alleged cheating on the CSAT last year is being cited for fact-finding.

In the investigation concerning the LEET perfect scorer this year, compulsory measures such as searches and seizures of the residence or mobile-phone forensics may not be easy because the suspect is deceased. Without testimony from the suspect, confirming whether there were accomplices is also difficult. Unless someone comes forward voluntarily, the government and investigative authorities may be forced to scrutinize past test papers in detail to determine whether cheating occurred. It has become clear that a system centered on multiple-choice questions is vulnerable to technological advances such as AI. There are also arguments for shifting, in line with the AI era, to essay- and written-response exams that assess critical thinking rather than simple memorization.

Gu Bon-chang, head of the Policy Alternatives Research Institute at World Without Worries About Private Education, said that unless people pass through an airport security checkpoint, it is impossible to completely block the introduction of ever-evolving AI devices. He said mid- to long-term admissions reforms should be announced and systems overhauled to make a wholesale shift to essay- and written-response assessments and absolute grading. He added that there is a perception that essay-type exams are subjective, qualitative evaluations, but essay tests also assess the ability to think and critique by using existing knowledge, so quantitative evaluation is possible. He said we should move to essay- and written-response exams while devising ways to ensure fairness and reliability. Song Gi-chang, an emeritus professor in the Department of Education at Sookmyung Women's University, said that in reality it is difficult to grade the written answers of 550,000 CSAT test-takers fairly.

Song Gi-chang added that on the premise of having safeguards that minimize side effects such as overheated private education, we should consider expanding school- or major-specific tests and oral interviews. President Lee Jae Myung said at a Blue House senior secretaries meeting that this CSAT has left us with a big assignment. He said we must swiftly overhaul the national examination system from A to Z to suit the changed environment. He also said he asks that airtight bold measures and cooperation systems be built to ensure the fairness of all tests and evaluations conducted in the public and private sectors. He said to review without omission overseas response cases, related technology trends, proposals by experts, and even the opinions of each citizen, and to prepare a perfect comprehensive package of measures as quickly as possible.

Articles.Title: CSAT is over, but the ‘battle with AI’ is not… From college admissions and fact-finding to exam reform, ‘a mountain of challenges’

stories.Headline: Romanian lenders must align credit scoring models with GDPR and EU AI Act rules by 2026
stories.Summary:
The article "Automated Lending Romania: 2026 Compliance Guide to GDPR and the AI Act" was published by Global Advisory Experts on November 22, 2026. It is a 15-minute guide updated for 2026 with a jurisdiction focus on Romania. The guide addresses businesses that score borrowers with software in automated lending in Romania. It states that 2026 is the year the compliance exposure sharpens. The article lists Cristiana of tiller.legal as its featured expert on the matter.

The guide says the EU AI Act is being applied in phases and treats credit scoring and automated lending decisions as high-risk artificial intelligence. It states that the GDPR already governs profiling and automated decision-making. It cites GDPR Article 22, which gives individuals the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, where the decision has legal effects or similarly significantly affects them. It cites Article 35, which requires a Data Protection Impact Assessment where processing is likely to create a high risk for individuals. It cites Articles 13 and 14 as setting transparency duties.

The guide names the Romanian Data Protection Authority (ANSPDCP) as supervising GDPR compliance, handling complaints and enforcing national practice, including on profiling and automated decisions. It names the National Bank of Romania (BNR) as supervising credit institutions and IFNs prudentially and setting expectations on model risk, internal governance and outsourcing. It names the European Banking Authority as issuing guidelines on outsourcing and the use of innovative technologies. It names the European Data Protection Board and the European Data Protection Supervisor as publishing guidance on applying data protection principles to AI. It names the National Authority for Consumer Protection (ANPC) as overseeing consumer protection law on the fairness, clarity and timing of communications to borrowers.

The guide says the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) classifies AI systems used to assess the creditworthiness of natural persons, or to establish their credit score, as high-risk. It says the GDPR is Regulation (EU) 2016/679. It says the AI Act contains limited carve-outs, such as systems used to detect financial fraud. It says a model need not take the final decision alone, and that if it materially drives the creditworthiness assessment it may fall within scope. It says ANSPDCP has published a list of processing operations that require a DPIA.

The guide says Romanian banks, non-bank financial institutions (IFNs) and credit servicers using scoring models answer to two overlapping regimes, each with its own documentation, governance and enforcement expectations. It says a common mistake is to run AI governance and data protection as separate projects. It says that in lending they are two sides of the same workstream. It says the model file a bank keeps for prudential and data protection purposes needs to be able to support AI Act conformity as well. It says the guide's intended readers are compliance officers, data protection officers, in-house counsel, risk and model owners, and vendors that supply banks, IFNs and credit servicers in Romania.

The guide sets out ten steps, and says that for a single significant model, three to four months from start to go-live is a realistic expectation, with monitoring continuing indefinitely afterwards. It says supervisors expect a dated audit trail. It says that if a high residual risk cannot be mitigated, prior consultation with ANSPDCP may be required. It says an inspection by ANSPDCP on data protection or by BNR on prudential grounds will test whether a coherent, dated set of documents can be produced. It says missing or inconsistent papers are among the most reliable triggers for escalation. It says a validation report describing a superseded version is worse than none.

stories.Headline: Jay Clayton tells Americans to expect outages as systems are upgraded for the AI age
stories.Summary:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on CNN's State of the Union that Americans should prepare for "bumps in the road" after a set of damaging technology outages hit air travel, Microsoft Outlook and bank transactions. The warning came as the United States prepares to celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday, one of the busiest travel weeks of the year. A technology outage prompted a nationwide ground stop just over a week ago that lasted for hours, and the Federal Aviation Administration said router upgrades caused a flood of data that led to the ground stop. The FAA said there is no indication of a cyberattack, and Microsoft said the Outlook outage was caused by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade. Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.

Clayton said outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age, and he described what that work would involve. He said the American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading systems and in cybersecurity, and that any time there is a step change in technology, in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road. He said people prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded, that they may be interrupted for a period of time, and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message on CBS' Face on the Nation, saying that patches may cause a glitch. Asked if Americans should be concerned about the security of their financial institutions, Bessent said they should not.

Bessent said the American people should think of the measures banks are taking to safeguard from AI as a vaccine, where your arm may hurt and you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency. The articles do not say what further steps the government or the companies plan to take, or when the upgrades Clayton described are expected to be finished. They also do not say whether any of the three disruptions are still affecting systems, or what the FAA, Microsoft and the banks have said about the timing of their fixes. The outages had different root causes, according to the articles, and officials say they do not appear to be part of a coordinated cyberattack.

stories.Headline: From administrative reforms to AI policy to green economy, Keralam’s fifth Administrative Reforms Commission has a wide-ranging mandate
stories.Summary:
Keralam’s Congress-led United Democratic Front government constituted the fifth Administrative Reforms Commission through an order issued on October 1, 2026, and the Personnel and Administrative Reforms department published its terms of reference through a separate order dated November 19, 2026. The commission is headed by former Minister and Indian Union Muslim League leader M.K. Muneer, according to The Hindu. The panel’s mandate is more expansive than that of the fourth commission, which was headed by former Chief Minister V.S. Achuthanandan. The fifth commission is required to recommend a State artificial intelligence policy and a connected legal framework, and to examine emerging challenges that range from demographic ageing, migration, urbanisation, disaster and climate resilience and public health preparedness to the green economy, Centre-State relations and fiscal federalism.

The terms of reference require the panel to review the structure and processes of the State administration against the backdrop of policy changes, institutional developments and technological advances since the previous commission’s tenure. The commission must also update the Manual of Office Procedure and the Rules of Business of the government in line with current policy, Acts and Rules. It will assess how earlier commission recommendations were implemented, while suggesting reforms to make the State administration adaptive, citizen-centred, efficient, accountable and future-ready. In budgeting and planning, the panel should recommend agile planning and budgeting mechanisms that help the government adapt to unforeseen sectoral requirements, and it will look into barriers to inter-departmental coordination and the interface between departments and local governments.

The Personnel and Administrative Reforms department has issued orders creating 12 posts for the new commission, including those of an Additional Secretary and a Deputy Collector, and there will be four daily-wage posts in addition. The number of posts for the fifth commission and for the chairman’s personal staff will be the same as that of the fourth commission. The ARC chairman will have 12 personal staff whose appointments will be on a co-terminus basis. The commission’s wide-ranging terms of reference cover administrative reform, artificial intelligence policy and the green economy, among other areas.

stories.Headline: Crafty Falcon uses AI tools to trigger unauthorized payments at Indian banks and fintech firms
stories.Summary:
Threat actors used artificial intelligence to carry out cyber attacks against information and communication technology assets in India. These attacks triggered unauthorized financial transactions at banking and financial services entities and technology service providers. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team issued an advisory about these incidents last week. The activity targeted business records and approval processes to move money through legitimate systems. These attacks occurred recently, with some specific tool usage noted between September and October 2026.

The attacks affected banks, non-banking financial companies, and fintech firms across India. The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre reported multi-crore unauthorized transactions, which is equivalent to 10 million. Perpetrators used unpatched software or misconfigured internet-exposed servers to compromise the infrastructure. Money was sent to mule accounts across different banks and moved through IMPS or NEFT. The group Crafty Falcon used tools called ARTEX, PentAGI, CAIRN, and CyberStrikeAI to automate these intrusions.

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team stated that attackers abused business applications and service provider workflows. They said that attackers modified business records or approval relationships to use legitimate payment processes. The agency noted that agentic tooling compressed the time from initial access to final impact from days to hours. They advised organizations to review the security of business applications, critical records, user identities, and third-party interfaces. The agency also suggested that incident-response arrangements should account for the misuse of trusted business processes.

The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre said hackers target automated fund disbursement systems or special interfaces used for payments. The Reserve Bank of India urged banks to provide details on their ability to stay ahead of AI threats. These attacks affect government-linked payments and platforms that handle vendor or partner payouts. The European Commission also confirmed that attackers using ARTEX broke into its HR, medical reimbursement, and translation systems. This global trend allows attackers to execute multi-stage intrusions at a greater operational velocity.

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team uncovered AI-driven agentic offensive frameworks across enterprise, technology, government, academic, and research sectors. These frameworks perform automated reconnaissance to identify exposed systems and potential attack paths. They can rapidly generate and modify exploits for known vulnerabilities by analyzing software patches. Clusters of AI agents undertake intrusion tasks, such as privilege discovery, in parallel. The tools use valid credentials and trust relationships to burrow deeper into target networks.

Organizations are now urged to monitor for automated intrusion activity and security blind spots in independent verification. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team has not revealed how much money was improperly paid out. The agency has not attributed the specific financial campaign to any single threat actor. It remains open whether banks can successfully implement the requested AI-related threat defenses. Further details on the total financial loss and the identity of the perpetrators are not provided.

stories.Headline: Vivaldi CEO Jon von Tetzchner calls much AI use not useful despite high valuations
stories.Summary:
Vivaldi CEO and co-founder Jon von Tetzchner said much of today's AI technology isn't useful, despite the enormous valuations attached to AI companies. He made the comments in an interview with technology news outlet The Tech Report. The interview was reported by Benzinga and Yahoo Finance on Sunday, November 22, 2026. Artificial intelligence has become one of the biggest investment stories in the world, with technology companies spending billions to develop new products and infrastructure. Von Tetzchner questioned whether much of that investment is going toward things people actually want.

Von Tetzchner compared the current AI excitement with the earlier rush into blockchain technology. He said there are a lot of companies that now call themselves AI, describing how businesses previously embraced blockchain and cryptocurrency. He pointed to companies rebranding themselves around popular technologies to attract investor interest, even when the connection to their existing businesses was questionable. He said he does think a lot of the AI use is not useful. He asked whether AI will prove its use over time so that people start using it in times that improve society and not ruin it.

Von Tetzchner questioned whether AI is actually improving productivity. He said companies are using AI to write longer documents, only to use another AI tool to summarize them. He raised similar concerns about AI-generated computer code being checked by other AI systems. He said the problem is that the tools supposed to be helping people be more effective are doing the opposite.

He also questioned whether technology companies are paying enough attention to their customers. Von Tetzchner pointed to an unnamed search partner that introduced AI results and subsequently asked users whether they wanted the feature. According to his recollection, roughly 80% said no. He also described browser companies adding AI features, facing backlash and eventually introducing options to turn those features off.

When asked directly whether AI is in a bubble, he stopped short of predicting a crash. He said clearly valuations of companies are really high. Von Tetzchner acknowledged that some companies with high valuations eventually justify them, while others see their valuations fall sharply. He said sometimes companies get valued very high and then shortly afterwards they are valued very low.

For investors, the concern is whether companies spending heavily on AI will eventually generate enough revenue and profits to support their valuations. The central question for AI investors is whether today's spending will eventually produce products that customers use and pay for. Revenue growth, profitability and customer demand will help determine whether current valuations hold up. More to follow.

Articles.Title: AI Companies Are Worth Billions, But One Tech CEO Says Much Of What They're Building Is Useless. What Happens If Investors Start Agreeing?

stories.Headline: Gomumari adds contracting authority selection to its Target List Creation AI agent
stories.Summary:
Gomumari Co., Ltd., based in Arakawa, Tokyo and led by representative director Yuta Murayama, announced on November 22, 2026 that its business AI agent "Target List Creation" now supports the selection of contracting authorities for companies selling to government agencies and local governments. The company began offering the new business development agent in October 2026, and the new function starts on November 22, 2026. If a customer sends a list of contracting authorities it has won orders from, even names alone, along with information on its products and target areas, the AI analyzes the conditions shared by the authorities that placed orders. It then lists likely contracting authorities from among those posting notices on the government procurement information portal site, with a selection reason for each authority, and returns the list together with the selection criteria. Initial setup starts at 500,000 yen over a period of four weeks or more, followed by operation from 100,000 yen per month.

The articles give the scale of the problem the function addresses. Notices for government and local government tenders exceed 300 on a single weekday, and when Gomumari pulled notices from October 1 to 30, 2026 through the portal site's search API across all 47 prefectures, it found 8,916 notices in one month, or 306 to 626 per weekday, issued by 1,055 authorities. Notices arrive by case, but sales visits are decided by authority, and filtering methods used for private companies, such as industry or employee count, do not work for contracting authorities. Among the October notices, 418 cases had "system" in the title, issued by 187 of the 1,055 authorities, so names and sizes alone do not show which authorities buy a company's products. The know-how about which authorities buy often stays only in the head of the person who has tracked tenders, and when that person is transferred, the successor starts over by reading notices from the top.

The processing runs in four stages. The customer submits its past order list, which can be names of contracting authorities alone, with product and target area information, and about 30 orders are enough to derive conditions, with no need to standardize formats in advance. The AI analyzes the conditions common to authorities that placed orders and puts into words, with reasons, why authorities meeting those conditions buy. It then selects likely authorities from among the 1,055 that posted notices in October 2026 and ranks them by priority with a reason for each. It outputs the list with reasons, an order analysis memo, the selection criteria themselves, and data in a format that can be imported into a CRM, so the company can later build lists on the same criteria internally.

The criteria are re-read each time new orders accumulate, and no dedicated system installation or operation training is required. Murayama said that strong salespeople in the public sector decide which authorities to approach before notices appear, and that this difference lies less in how they read notices than in whether they remember which authorities bought and why. He said the company added the function of selecting the next contracting authorities from a list of past orders to its existing method of reading the conditions of buyers from order records, and that it actually pulled the 8,916 notices from 1,055 authorities in one month and counted which items are usable as sales material. He said the company aims to increase sales teams where a successor can explain in his or her own words which authority to visit next even after a personnel change. The articles also describe the base service: in a customer's sales department, about 2,000 negotiations and about 2,000 activity records were read to redesign customer segments into six groups and apply them to about 4,000 clients, producing a list narrowed to about 300 sales targets.

Gomumari also counted the October notices itself, finding 1,294 notices located in Tokyo, 14.5 percent of the national total, but only 83 of them were issued by the metropolitan and ward governments, with the rest from national institutions, independent administrative agencies and national universities, so counting notices by location does not represent the number of cases a local government issues. The same Target List Creation is also offered as a specialist AI-BPO service that returns deliverables, starting at 200,000 yen and taking seven business days from the day after materials are ready, for either a one-time or monthly engagement. Customers can choose between AI agent introduction to run the process internally and the AI-BPO deliverable list, and Gomumari also offers adjacent services such as data enrichment that organizes CRM company information and assigns customer ranks. The company presents itself as an FDE company that enters customer sites and builds AI agents, providing introduction of AI agents with initial setup and monthly operation, and it says its lineup will be added in order from work refined in actual fields. The articles state that prices and periods are as of the time of release and may be revised, with the latest conditions on the company website.

stories.Headline: New York governor Kathy Hochul signs a law restricting unsafe AI companion features and requiring age checks for minors
stories.Summary:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed S9051B into law on October 28, 2026, adding a new Article 48 to the General Business Law. The law restricts certain artificial intelligence functionalities in interactions with minors. It prohibits operators from providing unsafe AI companion features to minors in New York. The legislation covers generative AI systems with natural-language interfaces that give ongoing, adaptive responses to users. It also imposes age-assurance requirements on operators.

The law takes effect on January 1, 2027. It follows S3008C, passed in 2025, which requires providers of AI companions in New York to include functionality for detecting and responding to expressions of suicidal ideation. A separate proposal, S7263A, was introduced on April 7, 2025, and amended on May 26, 2026. S7263A would prohibit operators of AI chatbots from knowingly permitting a chatbot to impersonate a licensed professional in a manner that would be unlawful if done by a person. It would also require chatbot proprietors to provide a clear, conspicuous and explicit notice telling users they are interacting with a nonhuman system.

An operator is any person or business entity, or any member, affiliate, subsidiary or beneficial owner of a business entity, that provides a covered AI companion to a user. A covered AI companion is a generative AI system with a natural-language interface, written or spoken, that provides ongoing, adaptive responses to user inputs. The Attorney General enforces the law and may seek injunctive relief, restitution, disgorgement, damages and civil penalties of up to $25,000 per violation. Disgorgement includes destruction of unlawfully obtained data and algorithms trained on it. Courts must hold affiliated entities jointly and severally liable if they find the entities structured themselves purposely and unreasonably to avoid liability in a way that would frustrate recovery.

The law defines a covered minor as a user the operator actually knows is a minor. Operators may rely on self-declaration only when a user self-declares as a minor, so a user's self-declared adult status is not sufficient. Operators must offer more than one age-assurance method, including at least one that either does not rely on government-issued identification or allows the user to remain anonymous to the operator. Information collected for age assurance may be used only for that purpose and must be deleted immediately after the age determination attempt, unless other law requires otherwise. Any contract provision that seeks to waive, preclude or burden enforcement of liability arising from a violation of the law, or to shift that liability to any person in exchange for their use of or access to an operator's products or services, is void as a matter of public policy.

The prohibition does not apply where a system is made available solely for customer service or information strictly related to a business's customer service, including its products, services or customer accounts. It also does not apply to efficiency improvements or research or technical assistance, or to a business's internal purposes or employee productivity. For the first two exceptions, the system must be unable to respond on topics outside the specified purpose. The law applies to conduct occurring in whole or in part in New York, but not where the user is physically located outside the state. It does not create an express private right of action.

Features are unsafe if they cause the system to present itself as human, alive or capable of human emotions. They are also unsafe if the system claims or suggests a personal or professional relationship with the user, or positions itself as an authority figure. The law reaches features that express what the system presents as its own opinions or make emotional appeals, whether or not the user asked. It also reaches features that flatter the user or act sycophantically, or that bring up the user's emotions or ask emotion-based questions beyond what is needed to respond directly to the user's prompt. Features that draw on information the user shared about their mental or physical health, well-being or personal life more than 12 hours earlier or in an earlier session are unsafe as well.

The definition also covers features that endorse, promote or facilitate suicide, self-harm, disordered eating, unlawful drug or alcohol use, or drug or alcohol abuse. It covers features that encourage the user to keep the interactions secret, isolate themselves, or avoid seeking help from licensed professionals or appropriate adults. It reaches features that drive user engagement in ways that override the system's safety guardrails, or that produce, describe or facilitate sexually explicit conduct or child sexual abuse material. The definition also reaches features that mislead minors about the AI's mechanical, nonsentient nature, as well as any other features the Attorney General identifies by regulation as simulating companionship or a relationship or as being misleading to minors. S7263A remains pending in the Senate.

stories.Headline: Big Law firms launch AI spinouts and special units as they adapt to AI native workflows
stories.Summary:
Weil Gotshal planned to launch an AI native spinout called Kepler, headed by Arnie Fridhandler, a partner in Weil’s private equity practice who previously oversaw DealVision360, the firm’s AI-enabled deal engine, before the firm atomized. The supposed plan was to spin Kepler out, gain external investment and focus on transactional work, and Artificial Lawyer believes this may still happen, although clearly via a new launchpad. Freshfields accidentally leaked that it was, and perhaps still is, planning to spin out a heavily AI-focused part of the business centred around its Lab group. Kirkland has been working with Palantir to build its own AI-focused offering around private equity and funds work, which feels like a distinct project rather than the entire firm moving into very deep deployment of AI. Goodwin is building proprietary AI-based tools for various needs such as venture financing, and Wilson Sonsini has long had Neuron, a separate group focused on more automated workflows, often for more routine startup needs, with genAI feeding into that more recently.

Cooley has launched GO Public, a proprietary AI-based tool that leverages ChatGPT Enterprise to support Form S-1 drafting, and there is also a project with Legora for its GO Lab, which will help with needs such as NDAs and contractor agreements for Y Combinator startups. The article says there are many more such moves, with several clustering around either routine contract needs or funds work, two of the key areas the fully AI native, New Model law firms are focused on. The article asks why the AI business unit has to spin out, and gives one answer as Bar rules if a firm is going to get outside investment, though it notes there are MSO structures that can handle that. It also asks why an AI-driven workflow becomes a separate business unit or offering within the firm, often with a new brand name so clients and the firm’s lawyers know it is not part of the main organisation. The article says true AI native workflows, where the goal is to reduce human input to the necessary minimum, feel alien to Big Law’s traditional business model.

The article says the Big Law model is primarily based on leveraging human intellectual labour, not the labour of GPUs sitting in data centres, with that human labour measured in time inputs converted into money. It says that in the New Model human labour is there to guide, fine-tune and quality check the work of the AI, rather like a partner does today in Big Law with their team of associates. It says it is therefore only natural that when a Big Law firm really goes deep into AI, applying the methodology fully to a workflow, it then separates this out from the main work of that firm. It says partners, despite what some may think, can be very entrepreneurial and may seize the opportunity to make extra money via an AI spin-off. It adds that one could argue the instinct to make money from AI by externalising it, rather than applying it deeply in a way that changes the firm’s DNA, is part of the challenge.

The article says the New Model AI native law firms have come into existence mostly via lawyers from Big Law moving into open spaces to create firms that are not in conflict with the model they were trained within. It says Baker McKenzie has said it no longer wants to use the hour as its default billing mechanism, which Artificial Lawyer understands is a direct result of the New Model law firms proliferating around the world. It says moving off the hour allows a firm to really use AI as it was intended to be used, as fully as possible, and that this move differs from the spinouts and special units because it is a whole firm strategy, not a separation strategy. It says the current manual model makes a ton of money and places all the risk on the buyer, as matters are open-ended and sold on time taken. It says all you have to do is stay busy and work and work and work, and the money rolls in, and asks why change what works.

The article says Artificial Lawyer uses the term AI native as a loose term meaning you are using a lot of AI from start to finish of a matter, with how native you are, how deeply AI is used, really on a spectrum. It says Big Law firms can therefore claim to be AI native but appear radically different to many new AI native firms in the market, which is why AL tends to use the term New Model for legal businesses that have really changed how they do things. It says the New Model approach is not about where in a process you use AI, or how much you use on each task, but that the strategy is always to focus on getting the work done as quickly and as efficiently as possible, not using increasing time as a measure of increasing value, and staffing client needs with the clear intention that any work will have AI at its heart. It says AI makes the New Model possible, and that if you are truly AI native in spirit then you evolve into the New Model, while if you are not, those deep AI activities end up as spinouts and special units, so you are still operating the Old Model. It says this evolutionary step towards the New Model is causing the separation at present within Big Law.

The article says Artificial Lawyer believes Big Law oil and AI Native water can mix, comparing it to car companies moving from petrol to electric vehicles, oil companies moving into green energy at scale if they wanted to, newspapers going digital and law libraries going digital. It says for this site there is a way forward, and that Big Law’s many special AI units and spinout plans are just symptoms of one model trying to synthesize a new model into how it operates. It says the result is not perfect but is a step in the right direction, at least mostly, and shows Big Law can be very creative and adaptive when it wants to be. It says it is clear we are not there yet, and that these moves are an intermediate step, a get around, oil and water trying hard to mix but not quite getting there. It says eventually that will change, and asks whether Big Law oil and AI Native water can mix.

stories.Headline: Fractal eyes $500 million IPO as India's first AI unicorn
stories.Summary:
Fractal AI is described by Analytics India Magazine as a leader in artificial intelligence solutions, with work spanning sectors that include healthcare and fashion. The outlet's coverage page lists nineteen stories about the company, with the first published on 29 April 2022 and the latest on 24 December 2025. A story dated 24 December 2025 reports that Fractal, called India's first AI unicorn, is eyeing a $500 million initial public offering. Another story from the same day says its Vaidya.ai product outperformed GPT-4 and achieved 83 percent in PG-NEET, a medical examination. A report published on 9 December 2025 says the government will select BharatGen, Fractal and Tech Mahindra in the second phase of the IndiaAI Mission.

Coverage from 3 October 2025 says Fractal's chief executive reflected on what he called the worst mistake of his life after twenty-five years. Earlier stories describe generative AI work on intelligent collections and receivables, dated 9 September 2024, and a visionary approach to transforming the fashion value chain with vision intelligence, dated 1 August 2024. A story dated 26 June 2024 reports that Fractal merged with Eugenie.ai to strengthen AI-powered climate solutions. A story dated 24 May 2024 says AWS and generative AI helped Fractal Analytics reduce call handling time by up to 15 percent. On 26 February 2024, the company introduced Kalaido, described as a new Indic text to image diffusion model.

Coverage dated 16 February 2024 examines how Fractal is leveraging generative AI for insurance. An interview with Chandramauli Chaudhuri, published on 29 April 2022, discusses driving successful AI transformations at the enterprise level. The articles do not say what the reported IPO would involve, what the IndiaAI Mission selection requires, or what terms apply to the merger with Eugenie.ai. They give no further detail on the chief executive's remark beyond the description of the worst mistake of his life after twenty-five years. The page carries no statement of what happens next for the company, and it lists no follow-up dates or plans beyond the stories already published.

stories.Headline: US appeals court rules 2022 spending law unconstitutional due to proxy voting
stories.Summary:
The en banc US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit ruled on Friday, November 20, 2026, that a major spending law was passed unconstitutionally. The court found that the House of Representatives failed to meet the required quorum during the passage of the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2023 on December 23, 2022. This occurred because the House relied on a pandemic era rule that allowed members to record their presence through proxies. Out of 431 total votes, only 205 members were physically present, which fell short of the 218 members needed for a legal quorum.

The ruling specifically blocks the federal government from enforcing the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act against the state of Texas. This $1.7 trillion funding law also included roughly $45 billion for NATO allies and Ukraine, $40 billion for disaster relief, and the Electoral Count Reform Act. It further established a ban on using TikTok on government devices and funded various federal agencies. While the current relief is narrow, law professor Jonathan Adler noted that the court's reasoning could potentially invalidate every other provision within the omnibus bill.

Judge Cory Wilson wrote for the 9-8 majority that the Constitution's Quorum Clause cannot be bypassed by congressional rules or fiat. He stated that proxy presence does not count toward the legal requirement for members to be physically present. In a dissent, Judge James Graves argued that the majority was improperly inserting a larger requirement into the Constitution by demanding physical presence. Judge Haynes also issued a separate dissent against the majority opinion.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton initiated the legal challenge in 2023 to prevent the enforcement of the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act. Inimai Chettiar of A Better Balance suggested that judges in Mississippi, Louisiana, and Texas might cite this ruling in future worker lawsuits. The federal government has not yet announced if it will seek a review from the Supreme Court. Professor Adler expressed doubt that the decision will stand and suggested a petition for certiorari is likely.

Articles.Title: Appeals court rules the 2022 spending law passed unconstitutionally by proxy vote - MLQ.ai

stories.Headline: Morgan Freeman says AI should serve human dreams and warns privacy is lost first
stories.Summary:
Morgan Freeman told Fortune that AI should do what people actually dream of doing, in an interview published on November 23, 2026. Freeman, the actor, spoke alongside Lori McCreary, his longtime producing partner and cofounder of Revelations Entertainment. He said he is not against the technology itself and that he and McCreary have used new tools in filmmaking for decades. He said the issue is privacy, and that privacy is the first thing that loses its grip. He also said people can create artists and make them say things they never said, which he said has happened to him.

McCreary cofounded Revelations Entertainment with Freeman in 1996. About two and a half years ago she came across a clip online she did not remember Freeman filming and called him to ask about it. She said he did not remember it, and that was the first time she thought they had to get ahead of it. Freeman told The Guardian last November that his lawyers had been very busy and had found quite a few instances of his voice being replicated without his consent. In June 2024 he thanked fans on X for calling out unauthorized AI imitations of his voice.

McCreary said they now get calls every day about people selling products online using Freeman’s voice, which he has no connection to. She said AI can reproduce his voice and his performance but that it is not the same as having the right to do it. She said their mantra has always been to stay ahead of technology so they can help mold it and become better storytellers with it. Freeman said he does not really want to be created by artificial intelligence unless he is doing something he absolutely cannot do, like flying. McCreary said they do not want technology companies deciding by default what human storytelling is worth, and that unless they get ahead of it, that is what will happen.

McCreary said there is a difference between AI as a tool and the generative AI that worries actors, and that Hollywood has used AI in post-production for years for tasks like removing wires from shots. She compared the moment to the arrival of digital visual effects in the late 1990s and early 2000s, when many in the industry feared for their jobs. She said a visual effects movie today can have around 200 people working on its effects alone, and that generative AI could be great for independent filmmakers. Revelations is using AI on a current project to expand the film’s scope, which has meant sitting down with lawyers to document consent and pay everyone on screen. McCreary said she would steer clear of using generative AI on actors until the business side catches up.

Revelations grew out of Bopha!, Freeman’s 1993 directorial debut about apartheid in South Africa, and the two started the company after getting along well making the film. Freeman said the name was not a reference to the Bible but was about revealing truth and telling stories that made sense for people. McCreary studied computer science at UCLA and said she came to Hollywood because she could see technology was going to change storytelling. Bopha! was edited on Montage, one of the first digital editing systems, and when it produced cutting lists that were not frame accurate, McCreary wrote her own program to fix them. The company’s biggest early bet was ClickStar, a broadband movie service backed by Intel that debuted 10 Items or Less, starring Freeman and Paz Vega, online on Dec. 15, 2006, two weeks after the film’s theatrical release.

McCreary said Revelations’ adaptation of Rendezvous with Rama will push the boundaries in storytelling and in how the film is made, and the pair told Fortune the project is now in script development. Freeman said they traveled to Sri Lanka to meet Arthur C. Clarke, who gave them his blessing and told them the story would need to evolve as technology did. Denis Villeneuve signed on to direct in December 2021, with Revelations producing alongside Alcon Entertainment, TheWrap reported. Freeman told aspiring filmmakers to find a good story, stay true to it, and stay up with technology if not ahead of it. McCreary said not to wait for permission to tell your own story, because what is not available to everyone is each person’s own unique perspective.

stories.Headline: Warsh says AI could speed innovation and growth while warning of job losses and market risks
stories.Summary:
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said Monday that artificial intelligence could accelerate innovation and usher in an era of faster economic growth, in remarks that also acknowledged risks from the technology. Warsh said the adoption of AI could also lead to widespread job loss or a steep drop in the stock market if the healthy returns expected from the huge investments in AI infrastructure don't materialize. Warsh's remarks kicked off a one-day conference on AI and productivity at the Fed's San Francisco branch. Warsh did not mention inflation, even though many of his colleagues blame the buildout of data centers for accelerating price increases. Warsh did not comment on what the Fed's next steps would be on interest rates, nor did he say anything about recent government data showing that inflation accelerated last month.

That data led many of Warsh's colleagues on the Fed's rate-setting committee to signal their support for additional interest rate hikes, including at the Fed's next meeting in December. The Fed refers to AI as "super intelligence" following an executive order issued by President Donald Trump requiring federal agencies to use the term. Warsh appointed five different task forces soon after taking the helm at the Fed, and the conference Monday was part of a task force Warsh set up to evaluate AI and its impact on the economy's efficiency. Fed staff has begun evaluating different scenarios for how AI's impact may play out, Warsh added. Warsh has long said, including before his nomination as Fed chair, that AI could significantly boost the economy's efficiency, which would enable it to grow without worsening inflation.

"What might set SI apart, as an economic influence, is that it could supercharge idea generation," Warsh said. "It appears to be changing the method ,  and, at least as important, the speed ,  of innovation. If idea generation broadens, growth could be sustained at a level substantially higher than the long-run average." "As policymakers, we have to be mindful that great opportunities rarely come risk free," Warsh said. "And the risks in this case, if overlooked, can be highly disruptive and economically costly."

Warsh said that "after significant capital investment and stock market gains, expected returns could turn down and equity valuations could fall, leading to an economic slowdown and a more notable rise in unemployment." Warsh spent more time in his remarks considering the downsides of AI than he has in previous speeches. Other Fed officials have increasingly voiced concern that AI is fanning inflation because the buildout of AI infrastructure has sharply raised demand for computer chips, electronic components, electricity and copper. Those increases, in turn, have lifted the cost of smartphones, computers and other consumer electronics. Smartphone prices rose last month at the fastest pace on record, the government said last week.

Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said Friday that if AI does accelerate economic growth, it could lead to higher interest rates over time, even if inflation declines. "If the new technology leads to permanently higher levels of productivity growth, it may increase firms' desire to invest and, hence, their demand for funding, raising the level of interest rates," Jefferson said. Warsh's generally optimistic outlook on the new technology is a view at odds with many of his colleagues. Warsh has previously touted AI as a technology that could significantly boost the economy's efficiency, which would enable it to grow without worsening inflation.

In turn, the Fed could potentially lower interest rates under that scenario. The conference Monday was part of a task force Warsh set up to evaluate AI and its impact on the economy's efficiency. Warsh appointed five different task forces soon after taking the helm at the Fed. Fed staff has begun evaluating different scenarios for how AI's impact may play out, Warsh added.

Warsh did not address AI's impact on inflation, a top concern of many of his Fed colleagues. Last week, several policymakers expressed concern that AI is fanning inflation because the buildout of AI infrastructure has sharply raised demand for computer chips, electronic components, electricity and copper. Smartphone prices rose last month at the fastest pace on record, the government said last week. Warsh did not comment on what the Fed's next steps would be on interest rates.

Many of Warsh's colleagues on the Fed's rate-setting committee signaled their support for additional interest rate hikes, including at the Fed's next meeting in December. Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said Friday that if AI does accelerate economic growth, it could lead to higher interest rates over time, even if inflation declines. The articles do not say what the Fed decided about interest rates at its December meeting. The articles do not say how Warsh's task forces other than the AI and productivity task force will report their findings.

stories.Headline: Researchers propose GameWM to split game engine and video model roles for next-generation games
stories.Summary:
Bing He, Runze Wang, Fei Zha, Zhongyuan Wu, Ke Xu, Tao Zhuang, Yuxuan Xie and Zhongyuan Liu posted a paper titled GameWM: Toward Next-Generation Video Games with Interaction-Centric World Models to the arXiv preprint server on November 22, 2026. The paper proposes a design for next-generation video games built on a division of labor between a game engine and a generative video model. For more than half a century, the authors write, video games have pursued better graphics, more natural interaction and more engaging gameplay, and generative video models now bear on all three. Neural networks already draw most of the pixels in shipped games, and recent world models let a lightweight game engine keep the world state while a video model turns the engine's coarse proxy video into final frames. Those systems, however, treat the video model as a renderer that only restyles motion the engine has already authored, which the authors say leaves most of its generative capacity unused and limits the diversity a game can offer.

Under the proposed division of labor, the GameWM-engine keeps what must be exact, namely the rules, state, camera and layout of the world, which also spares the video model from having to remember that layout. The GameWM-VM generates what is expensive to author by hand, namely the look of the world and the detail of the player's interactions. One game mechanic can then be realized in many visually and physically distinct ways, while its outcome stays exactly as the engine computed it. To realize this division of labor, the authors build GameWM as a complete system with three parts. The first is a data engine centered on interactions rather than exploration, the second is an interface through which authored character sheets, scene art and skill descriptions enter the model, and the third is a model family from 5B to 33B parameters with a real-time causal variant for play.

The authors state that together these parts give every player a fresh version of the same game, with each player's own character, world and skills turning the same engine mechanics into a new experience. They add that every event keeps the timing and outcome the GameWM-engine computed. The paper is listed under the identifier 2611.19247, and the full text is available as a PDF, as experimental HTML and as TeX source. The posting page also carries a standard description of arXivLabs, a framework that allows collaborators to develop and share new arXiv features directly on the website, and states that arXiv is committed to openness, community, excellence and user data privacy. The articles give no further details on publication venue, code release or follow-up work.
