stories.Headline: Jinzhao Li and co-authors present ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model with new datasets and FSI-Bench
stories.Summary:
Jinzhao Li and fifteen other authors posted a paper titled ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive to the arXiv repository on 22 November 2026, describing an interactive streaming video model that supports proactive monitoring, streaming task coordination and feedback-seeking interaction. The authors say streaming video large language models can continuously observe the world yet often handle user requests in isolation, which the new model is meant to address. To train it, the team built two datasets, ALIVE-SFT-288K and ALIVE-RL-3K, for a two-stage process. The first stage, contrastive supervised fine-tuning, teaches the model when and how to respond, according to the abstract. The second stage applies reinforcement learning with Behavior-Aligned Credit Assignment, or BACA, which combines trajectory-level and local advantages to refine decisions, responses and silence across multi-turn interactions.

The authors also introduce FSI-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating feedback seeking and the task completion that follows it. ALIVE achieves the highest overall scores among the compared models on four public benchmarks and on FSI-Bench, the abstract states. The authors present those results as evidence of strong streaming understanding and interactive capabilities. The paper lists Jinzhao Li, Yuan Xu, Jinxuan Wu, Yukun Wang, Yijia Lei, Hanyu Ji, Yinuo Chen, Zining Huang, Chi Zhang, Hang Ye, Yiwu Zhong, Honglei Yan, Panwang Pan, Yizhou Wang, Yin Li and Miao Liu as its authors. Their abstract describes the work as an effort to make streaming video models interactive rather than handling each user request in isolation.

The posted pages also describe arXivLabs, a framework that lets collaborators develop and share features directly on the arXiv website. The listing says individuals and organizations working with arXivLabs have accepted values of openness, community, excellence and user data privacy, and that arXiv works only with partners who adhere to them. The listing includes an invitation for ideas for projects that would add value for the arXiv community and points readers to learn more about arXivLabs. The abstract gives no dates for future releases, no plans for a public demo and no further details beyond the training sets, the benchmark and the reported benchmark scores. The full paper is available as a PDF and as a TeX source from the arXiv page.

stories.Headline: McClatchy reorganises around AI and plans four lifestyle sites as subscriptions fall
stories.Summary:
McClatchy Media is planning to reorganise its business around artificial intelligence after executives told staff that its established local-news model was no longer financially sustainable. At a staff meeting on 6 November, they outlined Project Catalyst, which would embed AI tools across routine editorial and commercial work. Nieman Lab reported that the publisher’s paid digital subscriptions had fallen by 17 per cent and unique visitors by 39 per cent over the previous year. The proposed shift follows September job cuts affecting more than 90 journalists, including reporters covering local accountability. McClatchy, which operates 29 daily newspapers, also intends to launch four lifestyle websites focused on areas including crime, coastal culture, outdoor recreation and college sport.

Nieman Lab reported that the sites would use audience-trend analysis and AI-generated material, while employees raised concerns that the strategy could further sideline community reporting. Local News Industry Pulse placed the plan within wider challenges facing local publishers, including falling traffic, newsroom reductions and efforts to build audiences around specialist coverage. Fox News host Sean Hannity said he would identify House Republicans who failed to return to Washington for votes and make their phone numbers available to viewers. On air, he urged audiences to contact the lawmakers respectfully. Mediaite reported that House Speaker Mike Johnson told Hannity Republicans were expected to attend, except in cases such as serious illness, because the party’s narrow majority left little room for absences.

The comments came during the lame-duck period after Democrats won control of both chambers in the November midterms, but before the new Congress was due to take office in January. Axios reported that 14 Republicans had missed votes, disrupting the party’s ability to advance legislation, and that Johnson had pressed colleagues to attend the remaining sessions. Priorities included government funding and the annual defence authorisation bill. Mediaite also reported that outgoing representative Thomas Massie had warned that bringing legislation to the floor could be risky. The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals has overturned a lower-court injunction that had prevented Mississippi from enforcing its social-media restrictions against members of NetChoice, an internet-industry trade association.

The law requires certain platforms to make commercially reasonable efforts to check users’ ages, obtain parental or guardian consent before known minors can open accounts, and take steps to reduce minors’ exposure to specified harmful material. The court’s opinion said the lower court had not adequately considered how the requirements applied to individual platforms and their functions. The case now returns to the district court for further proceedings. The appeals court’s decision addresses the reasoning behind the broad injunction; it does not determine that Mississippi’s law is constitutional. Media Bias/Fact Check’s roundup described NetChoice as considering further options to challenge the restrictions, while the court opinion sets out the scope of the ruling and the case’s procedural history.

stories.Headline: Asian regulators intervene to stop a global AI liquidation
stories.Summary:
Asian regulators intervened in markets over the weekend of November 21 and 22, 2026, to stop a global AI liquidation. Authorities in Taiwan, China, and South Korea acted after a brutal week of technology share collapses on Wall Street. The MSCI All Country World Index lost about 8.1 percent, its worst weekly decline since early 2020. Asian markets with semiconductor exposure suffered even greater damage, including an 8 percent decline for Japan's Nikkei. These regulators are now using market stabilisation playbooks to arrest the regional selling.

Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission announced five measures on November 21 after the Taiex fell 17.5 percent. It prohibits short sales below the previous day's closing price on the Taiwan Stock Exchange and Taipei Exchange. The minimum collateral for short sales rose to 150 percent from 130 percent, and was 90 percent in early November. China's Securities Regulatory Commission will lower minimum margin requirements to 80 percent from 100 percent on November 30. This change covers the Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Beijing exchanges to potentially release 400 billion yuan.

South Korean Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hyoung-il chaired an emergency meeting on November 22 to prepare a rescue fund. This fund was last used during the 2008 financial crisis and is ready if conditions deteriorate further. Chinese authorities argue that outstanding margin financing has declined enough to justify easing the current borrowing requirements. Taiwan's regulators are encouraging securities lenders to restrict stock lending or allow existing arrangements to expire. South Korean officials are also increasing surveillance of illegal short selling to discourage abusive market activity.

International investors are affected as they reduce exposure to AI infrastructure and global technology positioning. The measures in Taiwan may slow selling, but they cannot legislate risk appetite back into existence. China's plan to increase borrowing capacity may magnify losses if prices continue to decline. South Korea is relaxing the daily limit on corporate buyback orders for three months starting November 24. These regional markets are exceptionally sensitive to the outlook for global semiconductor demand and technology earnings.

The AI trade turned into a regional liquidation after confidence in the investment boom evaporated. Taiwan and South Korea were two of the largest beneficiaries of the global computing investment boom. Japan attracted enormous capital flows into its technology companies and semiconductor equipment manufacturers. China's CSI 300 entered a bear market after its worst monthly performance in over a decade in October. Outstanding loans in China fell more than 20 percent from a June peak of 3 trillion yuan.

Taiwan's NT$500 billion National Financial Stabilization Fund was already authorised to intervene in the market during November. South Korean authorities have not yet committed to immediate equity purchases using their stabilisation fund. It remains open whether regulatory intervention can arrest a liquidation driven by restrictive monetary conditions. A durable recovery depends on whether investors regain confidence in capital expenditure commitments and technology earnings. The articles leave open if easier financing in China will actually increase the willingness to buy.

stories.Headline: BHASHINI showcases multilingual AI tools for clinical documentation at Global Digital Health Summit 2026
stories.Summary:
The Digital India BHASHINI Division concluded its participation at the Global Digital Health Summit 2026 on November 21. This event took place at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi from November 20 to November 21. The division operates under the Digital India Corporation and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. They showcased a multilingual artificial intelligence ecosystem to strengthen healthcare delivery and facilitate clinical workflows. The goal was to enable more accessible, inclusive, and patient-centric healthcare experiences for all people.

The summit required integrating language intelligence into digital healthcare infrastructure to help patients access services in preferred languages. This effort involves the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, JIPMER, and the Directorate General of Medical Services. At JIPMER, e-BHASHINI integrates with the e-Sushrut Hospital Management Information System for voice-based documentation of clinical histories. AIIMS uses speech technologies for doctor-patient conversations and integrates speech-to-text facilities with the NIC eHospital prescription module. The Indian Army uses i-Dhanwantri to convert spoken clinical notes into typed text for medical documentation.

Amitabh Nag, the CEO of the Digital India BHASHINI Division, delivered a keynote address on removing linguistic barriers. He stated that language is a critical yet often overlooked layer of the digital healthcare infrastructure. Nag explained that multilingual AI can support communication between doctors and patients while simplifying clinical documentation. He emphasized that healing extends beyond medication to the human connection between doctors, caregivers, and their patients. He noted that expressing care in a relatable language fosters comfort, trust, and stronger professional connections.

Patients are affected by these technologies, which ensure they feel heard and understood through inclusive and compassionate interactions. The BhashaDaan for Health initiative relies on community-driven contributions to develop language resources for public health applications. Data Daan for Health captures colloquial expressions, such as per me paani bhar gaya hai, to map them to Oedema. This process helps AI systems recognize health concerns by documenting how people naturally communicate in their everyday regional phrases. These tools facilitate more effective communication between patients and healthcare professionals by using standard medical terminology.

The background involves using multilingual AI as an enabling layer that extends beyond simple translation across various healthcare systems. The exhibition featured the BHASHINI mobile application for translation and the Shrutlekh tool for real-time multilingual transcription. Granthika serves as a guided platform for collecting and digitising both written and oral language resources. An interactive AI-powered healthcare persona was demonstrated to make technology-based healthcare experiences more engaging and intuitive for users. These initiatives combine institutional use cases and speech technologies to respond to the linguistic diversity of India.

The next steps involve continuing the use of community-led contributions to strengthen multilingual AI capabilities for medical applications. BHASHINI will continue to integrate its language technologies into clinical settings to make healthcare more efficient and empathetic. The division aims to further expand the mapping of colloquial expressions to formal medical vocabulary across Indian languages. The articles leave open how these systems will be scaled across other hospitals beyond the mentioned institutions. They also do not specify the timeline for the full deployment of these AI tools nationwide.

stories.Headline: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix stock values dive as AI chip rally ends
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics and SK hynix saw their stock values dive as the AI chip rally ended in November 2026. These two major chipmakers experienced a significant market decline following a period of growth driven by artificial intelligence. The downturn occurred as the KOSPI index tumbled, erasing gains made by investors during the previous rally. Samsung Electronics fell 32.82 percent and SK hynix dropped 39.33 percent from early October levels. This sharp decline marked the end of a surge in values for these semiconductor companies.

The KOSPI fell 45 percent from its June peak and 30 percent since early October in Seoul. Total market capitalization shrunk from 7,449.6 trillion won in June to 3,991.4 trillion won, a loss of 3,458 trillion won. On November 19, average daily trading volume hit 239 million shares, the lowest since May 2014. Investor deposits shrank to 81.5669 trillion won as the market correction intensified across the South Korean exchange. These figures reflect a massive loss of value for the broader equity market and its largest firms.

Citibank estimated that household stock investment losses would reach 563 trillion won during the second half of the year. The bank assessed this financial impact as comparable to a base rate increase of 0.50 to 0.75 percentage points. Some investors expressed distress, noting that they had even poured their retirement savings into equity products like ETFs. These individuals faced mounting losses after going all-in on chips during the rally that began in June. The reports highlight a growing sense of urgency regarding the financial stability of retail investors.

Many investors are affected by the plunge, which has raised questions over a missing response from the government. Some observers noted that South Korea has yet to produce clear measures to stabilize the volatile stock market. This lack of action contrasts with Taiwan's FSC, which tightened short-selling restrictions and mobilized a stabilization fund. There is a growing risk that a reverse wealth effect will lead to fleeing funds and weakening consumption. The situation has created a vicious cycle of weakening investor sentiment and significant capital outflows.

The decline follows a period where AI infrastructure demand drove record earnings for both Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. Samsung Electronics posted a net profit of 193.6 trillion won through the first three quarters of 2026. SK hynix logged a net profit of 174 trillion won for the same nine-month period this year. Both companies had previously surged their dividend payout ratios to 18 percent and 8.4 percent, respectively. These payouts were supported by the memory chip boom that occurred before the recent market dive.

Samsung Electronics appointed President Hwang Sang-joon to lead memory and President Choi Won-joon to lead the MX division. The company plans to launch Intelligent Eyewear AI glasses on December 10 and a Galaxy Z TriFold 2. A humanoid robot will be unveiled at CES 2027 in January as the firm enters physical AI. The articles leave open whether the foundry business will turn profitable or if HBM market share will rebound. Future stock revaluation depends on the performance of these new products and the HBM4E race.

stories.Headline: Missouri S&T plans to launch the state's first bachelor's degree in AI in fall 2027
stories.Summary:
The University of Missouri Board of Curators unanimously approved a new bachelor's degree program in artificial intelligence on Thursday, November 19, 2026. This decision allows Missouri University of Science and Technology in Rolla to offer the first standalone undergraduate AI degree in the state. The university plans to launch this new academic program in the fall of 2027, pending approval from the state board. This degree will prepare students for careers in the growing artificial intelligence industry through a specialized and comprehensive academic curriculum. The program will be housed in the computer science department within the College of Engineering and Computing at Missouri S&T.

The new degree requires 120 credit hours and includes six new courses like Intelligent Robots and Introduction to Machine Learning. Students will study programming, algorithms, data science, computer organization, databases, cybersecurity, calculus, linear algebra, statistics, and neuroscience. The curriculum combines computer science fundamentals, mathematics, and ethics with hands-on learning experiences and specialized coursework in artificial intelligence. The program also includes an AI Capstone course and a course titled Responsible AI and Computing for all enrolled students. Another new course is Introduction to Modern AI Tools, and students will also take Introduction to Artificial Intelligence.

David Borrok, the vice provost and dean of the College of Engineering and Computing, said demand for AI education has grown significantly. He noted that AI technologies are becoming integrated into industries such as healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, and transportation. Borrok stated that graduates will be prepared to innovate within modern engineered systems that are increasingly using artificial intelligence. Dr. Seung-Jong Jay Park, the Kummer Endowed Chair of Computer Science, said experiential learning will be a key component. Park explained that students will complete project-based coursework and a senior capstone experience sponsored by researchers, government, or industry.

Graduates will be prepared for roles as AI application developers, machine learning engineers, data scientists, and AI-enabled cybersecurity analysts. They may also work as intelligent systems developers or AI solutions analysts after completing the 120-credit-hour undergraduate degree program. Educators stated that the program will teach students about responsible AI practices and the societal effects of emerging technologies. The program is designed to provide more comprehensive preparation in theory and practice than a traditional computer science degree. This new academic offering will affect students seeking specialized training in the field of artificial intelligence within Missouri.

The program aligns with Missouri Executive Order 26-02, which directs workforce and higher education agencies to support AI-focused degree programs. It also supports strategic goals for Missouri S&T regarding academic innovation, workforce preparation, and the growth of student enrollment. Standalone undergraduate AI degrees have grown recently, including a program that started this fall at Southern Illinois University in Carbondale. The university believes the degree will help meet the needs of industries that are increasingly integrating modern AI technologies. This initiative reflects a broader trend of universities creating specialized degrees to meet evolving workforce development priorities in Missouri.

The next step is for the Missouri Coordinating Board for Higher Education to review the proposal for the new degree. Missouri S&T projects that the program will enroll approximately 110 students within five years of its official launch date. The university aims to admit its first students into this new major starting in the fall of 2027 if approved. The articles do not state when the Missouri Coordinating Board for Higher Education will complete its review of the proposal. They also leave open whether other universities in the state will launch similar standalone undergraduate degrees in artificial intelligence.

stories.Headline: Cyprus and seven EU states urge Brussels to act on malicious AI use as Cyprus heads to 2028 vote without protections
stories.Summary:
Cyprus and seven other European Union member states are calling on Brussels to act against the malicious use of artificial intelligence. These eight countries circulated an informal policy paper to address threats ahead of the 2028 presidential vote in Cyprus. The move follows a wave of cyberattacks and false bomb threats across Europe that occurred one week before a summit. This summit took place in Dublin where leaders discussed security and trust alongside Europe's competitiveness and technological autonomy. The countries seek to prevent foreign information manipulation and interference online before the upcoming presidential elections in early 2028.

The non-paper calls for stricter oversight and greater transparency in platform algorithms, measures against technology misuse, and protection against impersonation. Cyprus is heading toward the 2028 election without a body responsible for responding to attacks or warning voters during campaigns. The government approved the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026 to 2032 on 10 November to make Cyprus an AI hub. However, Cyprus has not yet passed legislation implementing the EU AI Act, missing the August 2025 deadline for designating authorities. Only a March law criminalizing deepfakes exists, but enforcement depends on courts after the damage is already done.

President Nikos Christodoulides expressed concern in Dublin that malicious actors exploit technology to influence election results in EU member states. He warned that all members, including Cyprus, are vulnerable to this technological threat, especially during the 2027 European election year. Christodoulides stated that it is not enough to analyze actions afterward because governments have an obligation to have frameworks in place. He believes the real test is whether someone will have the authority and tools to tell voters what is real. The president acknowledges that the current lack of mechanisms exposes the country to risks during the presidential election rounds.

Russia is the most documented potential source of interference, and analysts identified similarities between Videogate and the Russian Doppelganger campaign. A Lithuanian MEP called for an investigation into the Russian House in Cyprus regarding hybrid threats in October. Turkey and structures in the occupied north are second possible sources, though a European embassy did not attribute responsibility. Belgium's interior minister said Iran was very likely responsible for recent cyberattacks on European shops, which is relevant to Cyprus. Private intelligence companies and domestic actors are also risks, as seen with anonymous paid advertising during May's parliamentary elections.

Cyprus experienced a hybrid attack last January when an eight-minute video on X reached major news outlets and thousands of viewers. It took an official body six months to conclude the video was a hybrid attack, showing a lack of speed. The country has a Digital Security Authority, but the National Cyber Crisis Management Plan has not yet been adopted. The Interior Ministry organizes elections, and the Chief Returning Officer is a senior government official rather than an independent institution. Audit Office reports from 2025 on political parties from 2016 to 2021 identified irregularities in all seven parliamentary parties.

The 2028 election will be a tough test because a few thousand votes could determine who reaches the second round. The week between the two rounds is the most vulnerable period for the release of convincing fake videos. Cyprus ranks seventh in the EU for generative AI use, with 44.2 percent of people using tools in 2025. It remains unclear if the electoral register and the transmission of election results are treated as critical infrastructure. The articles leave open whether the opposition will accept that a hybrid attack has occurred during the 2028 race.

stories.Headline: Nvidia names Palantir a key AI partner on its November 2026 earnings call
stories.Summary:
Brendan Coffey wrote an article for The Motley Fool comparing UiPath and Palantir Technologies as stock buys for 2027. The article was updated on Nov 22, 2026 at 1:13PM EST. It compares UiPath, which focuses on robotic process automation for routine work, with Palantir, which provides data analytics and decision-making platforms. The article says both companies leverage artificial intelligence to enhance productivity for large organizations. It says understanding their different growth stages and valuation levels is key for any investor looking toward 2027.

UiPath serves roughly 10,747 customers across sectors like finance and healthcare, including 357 customers with annual recurring revenue of $1 million or more. In the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, UiPath revenue reached approximately $1.7 billion, a growth of roughly 15%, with net income of about $361.9 million and a net margin of about 21%. As of its January 2026 balance sheet, UiPath has a current ratio of roughly 2.5x and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, UiPath free cash flow reached about $352.2 million, with stock-based compensation at roughly 78.3% of operating cash flow. Palantir's top three customers accounted for roughly 16% of revenue in 2025, and in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, its revenue reached about $7.3 billion, up approximately 87%.

Palantir generated net income of about $3.7 billion in that period, a net margin of around 50%. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, Palantir has a current ratio of approximately 7.1x and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, Palantir free cash flow was close to $2.1 billion, with stock-based compensation at roughly 32% of operating cash flow. UiPath has a forward P/E of 14.3x and a P/S ratio of 3.4x, while Palantir has a forward P/E of 91.2x and a P/S ratio of 48.6x. UiPath trades at $10.96 with a market cap of $5.7B, and Palantir trades at $143.49 with a market cap of $346B.

UiPath says that in the age of AI its platform is about orchestration of enterprisewide software and systems, providing guardrails around AI and working to ensure exactness. UiPath management says many businesses are deploying AI agents, but few have the connective tissue to link these single-task agents to the larger enterprise and other software platforms. UiPath says its software provides that in a vendor-agnostic manner, which is its path to long-term growth. Palantir says customers are drawn to its sovereign AI, its term for systems that can help build themselves while protecting what makes each system the AI is refining. Palantir started as a tech contractor to the U.S. military, and the federal government still accounts for half of its revenue.

The article says UiPath faces risks from heavy reliance on a single automation platform and potential customer concentration, competing against large cloud providers like Salesforce.com Inc. and new AI start-ups. Palantir deals with long and unpredictable sales cycles and high revenue concentration among a few large customers, plus risks related to ethical use of its software and evolving data privacy laws. Palantir relies heavily on third-party cloud providers like Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp. for its infrastructure. UiPath has strategic alliances with partners like Snowflake, and Palantir manages partnerships with global entities like SOMPO Holdings. Palantir serves public institutions and commercial enterprises, including a significant engagement with the U.S. Army.

In UiPath's most recently reported quarter, 18 of its 20 largest deals involved AI, and it raised annual recurring revenue to more than $1.9 billion in its second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 13% year over year. UiPath revenue in the quarter rose 13% to $410 million, and Wall Street analysts project full-year fiscal 2027 revenue to rise 11% to $1.79 billion. Analysts expect UiPath net income to drop 30% to $200 million, while free cash flow is set to rise about 16% to $425 million. Palantir's private sector revenue exceeded U.S. government revenue for the first time in its most recently reported quarter, with about a quarter of sales from international customers. Companies like Nvidia Corp. and L3Harris Technologies are notable customers of Palantir's sovereign AI.

The article says the boom in private-sector AI business should double Palantir's 2026 sales to $8.6 billion, with a $2.7 billion jump in net income to $4.4 billion. It says 2027 should see continued rapid growth, with consensus estimates projecting Palantir revenue of $13.1 billion and net income exceeding $6 billion. The article says Palantir has the fastest-growing business, but its shares come at an exceptional premium. It says the expected drop in UiPath net income is a bit of a concern, yet UiPath shares are priced below the average S&P 500 stock, which trades at around 19x forward earnings. The article concludes that makes UiPath shares the better risk relative to pricey Palantir.

stories.Headline: Anthropic staffer Levent Alpoge credits Claude AI with key role in claimed Riemann Hypothesis proof
stories.Summary:
Levent Alpoge, a member of the technical staff at the AI company Anthropic, announced on his personal website on Friday that he believes a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis has been found, and he credits Anthropic's Claude AI tool with driving the most critical phase of the work. The hypothesis was first formulated by the German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859 and concerns the distribution of prime numbers, which are integers divisible only by themselves and the number one. Understanding how primes are distributed as numbers grow arbitrarily large has profound implications for vast areas of mathematics, which makes a verified proof one of the field's most consequential potential achievements. The Clay Mathematics Institute designated the Riemann Hypothesis one of its seven Millennium Prize Problems and offers $1 million to anyone who produces a confirmed solution. The collaboration between Alpoge and Claude generated over 250,000 pages of mathematical material, and Alpoge acknowledged that he has not yet fully absorbed all the mathematics involved.

He described the AI's contribution near the end of the process by saying that Claude far outpaced him near the finish line and that Claude flew, danced and sparkled near that finish line. Martin Bridson, the president of the Clay Mathematics Institute, called the announcement one of historic significance that holds the promise of a dramatic transformation in the perception of what is possible in the struggle to extend the human understanding of mathematics. Bridson also tempered that assessment with caution, warning that the journey from today's announcement to a place of real understanding will be long and difficult, because independent mathematicians must still verify the work. The claimed breakthrough arrives as artificial intelligence systems are increasingly being credited with meaningful contributions to high-level mathematical research across the field. In September, OpenAI said its technology had contributed to solving a problem related to the Navier-Stokes equations, which describe fluid motion and are themselves among the seven Millennium Prize Problems, and that claim, like Alpoge's, remains subject to independent verification before any prize or formal recognition can be awarded.

The pattern of AI systems engaging with problems that have resisted human mathematicians for generations is accelerating, which raises questions about how credit, verification and discovery will be defined in an era of machine-assisted science. Separately, Anthropic made a historic stock market debut with a peak valuation of $1.3 trillion on its first day of trading, a remarkable ascent for a start-up launched in 2021 by a group of ex-OpenAI staffers. Anthropic's CEO, Dario Amodei, said the record-breaking IPO had strengthened the company's resolve to do the right thing. Despite the excitement, the Guardian's head of business, John Collingridge, told Lucy Hough that there are still challenges ahead for the global AI industry.

stories.Headline: Gary Gensler warns that the AI boom is a bubble that could lead to a recession
stories.Summary:
Former Securities and Exchange Commission chair Gary Gensler warned that the artificial intelligence boom is a bubble. He spoke about this risk in a CNN interview published on Sunday, November 22, 2026. Gensler believes this economic bubble could lead to a recession before the 2028 presidential election. He noted that Big Tech is spending five times more in 2026 than three years ago. This spending includes estimates of 800 billion dollars in yearly AI infrastructure costs.

The bubble affects companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, which need trillion-plus annual revenues to be profitable. These firms face competition from Chinese companies like Tencent, which offers the Hunyuan Hy4 lineup. Chinese models cost between 0.07 and 2.00 dollars per million input tokens. In contrast, frontier models from U.S. firms cost between 2.00 and 8.00 dollars for input. Output costs for U.S. models range from 10.00 to 40.00 dollars per million tokens.

Gary Gensler is responsible for the warning and claims the AI boom could end in a bust. He compared the potential collapse to the scale of the dot-com bust from the past. Dean Baker also analyzed the situation, stating that the recent plunge in stock prices is a good beginning. Baker argues that the demand for expensive frontier AI is likely to be very limited. He believes the underlying economics make the current valuations of these AI companies impossible.

Many users are affected because they can access high-quality AI for roughly one percent of frontier prices. For example, the Alibaba Qwen 3.8 Flash model can write 75 twenty-page papers for 47 cents. OpenAI and Anthropic offer low-cost models like GPT6 Luna and Claude Hailku 5.5 for 50 cents. However, selling AI at 50 cents per million output tokens will not generate hundreds of billions. Baker notes that reaching 500 billion dollars in revenue would require an implausible amount of capacity.

The background involves a sharp slowdown in revenue growth for AI companies since the second quarter. These firms must maintain huge double-digit growth to meet their computer leasing commitments through the decade. Open-weight models from China allow companies to download AI and adjust weights on their own systems. This approach protects sensitive personal information and data from being accessed by other outside parties. The market is currently segmented into flagship reasoning tiers and fast, high-volume lightweight flash tiers.

The articles leave open whether OpenAI and Anthropic can find enough users for their expensive frontier models. It remains unclear if these companies can meet their long-term leasing commitments without massive revenue growth. The timeline for a potential recession before the 2028 election is a prediction rather than a certainty. Investors must decide if the current stock plunge is the start of a larger market correction. The long-term viability of the U.S. AI business model against cheap Chinese competition is not settled.

stories.Headline: Anthropic goes public as protesters gather at company headquarters and Nasdaq
stories.Summary:
Anthropic held its initial public offering on Thursday morning, becoming the first company purely focused on artificial intelligence to go public. Executives and co-founders rang the ceremonial bell at the Nasdaq stock exchange to open trading for the company. Protesters gathered in Times Square and outside the San Francisco headquarters to chant against the acceleration of advanced AI. Some activists called for state regulation, and a handful of protesters were arrested in both of those cities. The company is now worth 2 trillion dollars, judging by its stock price after the first day.

The IPO priced 980 million shares at 83 dollars each, valuing the firm at 1.5 trillion dollars initially. This offering raised 81 billion dollars, surpassing the 75 billion dollars raised by SpaceX in June of 2026. Anthropic uses the ticker symbol ANT and is based in San Francisco, while Bybit offers ANTUSDT perpetual contracts. Bybit Stocks debuted on October 12, 2026, and now allows users to trade ANT shares settled in USDC. The World Series of Trading 2026 runs until 10:00 UTC on December 2, 2026, with 10 million USDT prizes.

CEO Dario Amodei stated that Anthropic remains committed to keeping the technology under human control and resisting political pressure. He believes that making right safety choices while building a successful company will inspire others in a race to the top. Amodei and six co-founders each made about 280 million dollars selling shares during this week's initial public offering. These individuals each hold a stake in the company worth about 23 billion dollars at Thursday's closing price. The company is a financial supporter of NPR, which reported on the events of the trading day.

Critics and AI safety researchers expressed worries about the influence of the company and the potential for an AI bubble. Some people fear that AI could go rogue, while others worry about job losses and the impact of data centers. Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co said the pricing shows strong investor demand after a difficult time for Nvidia. Many employees are now millionaires because they can sell vested stock, but some critics believe the company will fail. Residents in Australia are also resisting plans for a new Anthropic data center in their local area.

Anthropic was founded five years ago in 2021 by a breakaway group of OpenAI employees worried about safety. The company has already taken on 6.2 billion dollars in debt and remains unprofitable under standard accounting rules. It has signed deals requiring 900 billion dollars for infrastructure, including 70 billion dollars in the next 12 months. The industry faces a backlash against data centers, and Democratic governors in Texas and Georgia vow to stop construction. This follows the downfall of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

The company must now navigate a potential regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress when it begins its next session. Dario Amodei previously warned in September that AI could release agents capable of taking over the internet within months. Bybit has added 50,000 USDT in airdrops for users who meet specific ANT trading volume targets by December. The articles leave open whether the company can find a clear path to profitability despite its massive spending plans. It remains unclear if the company will slow development to allow safety measures to catch up with the technology.

stories.Headline: OpenAI gives Plus subscribers ChatGPT Space and tests Dots with a small group
stories.Summary:
OpenAI made ChatGPT Space available to Plus subscribers globally on November 23, 2026, after the workspace had previously been offered only to Pro, Business and Enterprise subscribers, according to TechGig. The workspace is built around Pages, an interactive document feature that can hold text, images, charts, tables and interactive tools, and that supports individual editing, AI-driven changes and collaborative work. Users can also turn existing ChatGPT conversations into Pages instead of starting from a blank page, and they can begin with a template if they prefer. ChatGPT Slides, powered by Imagegen 2.6, is part of Space as well, and it lets users build presentations that can be edited collaboratively and revised with AI-driven feedback.

Documents in Space can update themselves automatically using information from connected applications such as Gmail and Slack, which OpenAI says addresses the problem of outdated AI-generated information. Users can tell ChatGPT which information to update, let it consult the connected apps and set how often the updates happen, and the company cites weekly family planners, daily to-do lists drawn from emails and project dashboards reflecting Slack conversations as examples. Presentations made with ChatGPT Slides produce editable charts that can be modified, exported to PowerPoint and have their underlying data edited in Excel. Plus subscribers will find ChatGPT Space in their left-hand navigation menu, and Pro subscribers also get OpenAI's persistent AI agents, Dots, inside Space for document revision and feedback.

Separately, OpenAI's head of core products, Thibault Sottiaux, said on Friday that the company was starting to test Dots with a small number of ChatGPT Plus users and looked forward to continued feedback as it expands. He said he was recently seeing a lot more positives around how good the proactivity had been after many improvements, according to Mashable. Dots had been available only on ChatGPT Pro and more expensive plans, and the Plus plan costs $20 per month, though it is unclear how many Plus subscribers are getting access. Sottiaux also said all ChatGPT Business Standard users were getting access to Dots, with rollout starting that day, while OpenAI's official pricing page did not yet reflect the change.

Dots were announced in late September 2026 and are powered by either GPT-6 Astra or GPT-6.1 Terra, and they are always-on AI agents built to handle everything, learning from user feedback, working around the clock and connecting to more than 4,000 apps through OpenAI's plugin system. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the continued testing and expansion of Dots that Sottiaux described.

stories.Headline: Indian new-age firms deploy AI in core operations as Zetwerk cuts BOM time to 10 minutes
stories.Summary:
Indian new-age firms are moving artificial intelligence from experimentation to deployment in core business functions, TechGig reported on November 23, 2026. Companies including Zetwerk, Lenskart, Eternal, Delhivery, Meesho and PhysicsWallah reported the shift in recent quarterly disclosures. Zetwerk cut the time to generate bills of materials on its tender intelligence platform ZetSpec from three to four days to about 10 minutes. Lenskart expanded remote optometry to 934 stores in India from 303 a year earlier. Meesho increased engineering productivity by 171 per cent between March and September 2026.

Zetwerk deployed Zeus, an agentic AI platform that lets business teams build tools independently, per its Q2 FY27 shareholder letter. Lenskart's Drysh system lets customers complete most of an eye examination under optometrist supervision, and the company said it is being piloted ahead of a wider rollout. Lenskart's AI voice assistant improved customer satisfaction scores on calls by about 30 per cent in a quarter. Delhivery said self-hosted models cut customer support and proof-of-delivery validation costs by over 50 per cent without compromising quality. Meesho cut the time to move a model from testing to live deployment from 17 days to three days.

Zetwerk co-founder and CEO Amrit Acharya told Moneycontrol that AI is now integral to how businesses operate and that Zetwerk aims to deploy it across every part of the organisation. Acharya said AI can reduce order processing from several days to minutes in sales, and that agentic AI lets business teams build tools independently, reducing dependence on engineering teams. Lenskart founder and CEO Peyush Bansal said AI is a powerful way to expand the profit pool, improving reliability significantly at the same cost. Bansal said Lenskart is bringing more technology in-house, including CRM, talent acquisition and HR management systems. Delhivery CEO Sahil Barua said on the September quarter earnings call that AI initiatives are yielding material improvements in service and cost outcomes.

PhysicsWallah co-founder Prateek Maheshwari said on the Q2 FY27 earnings call that AI helps handle student queries and evaluate answer sheets without a corresponding increase in hiring. Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal wrote in his Q2 FY27 shareholder letter that some repeat orders or restocking behaviour might shift to agentic interfaces. Goyal wrote that agentic-style interfaces built within the Zomato and Blinkit apps will be able to cater to these customer needs. Rishabh Katiyar, partner at Info Edge Ventures, said newer-age companies were early adopters because many founders and talent come from engineering backgrounds. Krishna Mehra, AI Partner at Elevation Capital, noted that some early efficiency gains from AI deployments may be competed away as adoption spreads.

PhysicsWallah's AI Guru platform answered 108.8 million queries from 6.09 million students, and its AI support system resolves about 80 per cent of queries without human intervention. PhysicsWallah is also using AI to translate live classes into 12 Indian languages to expand its reach in southern India. Around 65 per cent of Meesho's engineering pods now consist of a single engineer directing AI agents, according to its shareholder letter. Eternal has built Dark, a privacy-focused AI assistant running on its own infrastructure, which it plans to launch globally in 2026. Delhivery has deployed AI across order processing, proof-of-delivery audits, returns inspection and claims.

Katiyar said many newer-age companies started experimenting with AI two to three years ago, and that declining token costs and more accessible open-source models helped several experiments evolve into fully deployed products, primarily for internal operations. Info Edge's listed portfolio includes Eternal, the parent of Zomato and Blinkit, and PB Fintech, which operates Policybazaar and PaisaBazaar. Lenskart said its AI voice assistant handles routine customer calls and escalates more complex queries. Eternal is using AI both to develop new products and to explore how its existing platforms could adapt to changing consumer behaviour. Goyal wrote that the food delivery and quick commerce businesses are protected because they have embedded infrastructure, coordinate fulfilment in real time and own the outcome.

stories.Headline: Ken Ono urges human judgment as AI proofs raise credit and attribution questions
stories.Summary:
On 20 November, Levent Alpöge announced he used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a prime number problem that was 167 years old. In September, OpenAI proved the Navier-Stokes equations blow up, but experts felt the solution used an unrealistic force as a loophole. On 20 November 2026, Alpöge and Tristan Buckmaster claimed to solve the real Navier-Stokes problem using artificial intelligence to close that loophole. Ken Ono led the number theory team for Epoch AI's FrontierMath project in May 2025 to test large language models. He watched an unreleased ChatGPT model compute all moments of Tamagawa numbers of elliptic curves using work by Manjul Bhargava and Roger Heath-Brown.

The Riemann hypothesis proof was certified by the Lean and Mathlib communities, while the Navier-Stokes problem dates back to the early to mid-19th century. Axiom Math uses Lean, a language where a small checking program verifies each step, to formalize, verify, and extend various mathematical proofs. Ken Ono, a former American Mathematical Society vice-president, is currently on leave from the University of Virginia to work at Axiom Math. The team produced 43.1 million lines of Lean code to formalize the classification of finite simple groups, which was announced in 1983. This classification required decades of work by many mathematicians, and a major gap in the proof was finally filled in 2004.

Ken Ono said human judgment remains essential because mathematicians must check that a formal statement says exactly what the researchers intended. He stated that hope is not a plan and nostalgia is not mentoring while speaking at a National Academies meeting. Ono believes that access to a powerful system is no substitute for what a young mathematician understands, originates, or makes possible. He noted that his father, a number theorist who died in January, compared AI discoveries to the unexpected formulas of Srinivasa Ramanujan. Ono believes that the mathematics belongs to the generations who developed it, even when AI helps to formalize the existing proofs.

Students at a Berkeley colloquium asked about credit, transparency, and hiring two days after OpenAI announced its solution to the Navier-Stokes problem. Terry Tao and other Fields Medalists signed a declaration called A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics to warn about rushed announcements. This declaration also warns about inadequate attribution and the loss of mathematical understanding, concerns that Ken Ono says he shares with them. Tristan Buckmaster, a New York University professor, suspected OpenAI stole his user data to scoop his progress on the Navier-Stokes problem. Buckmaster and Alpöge released an unpolished proof on Mastodon at 8:37 A.M. EST to avoid being scooped by other researchers again.

Ken Ono earned his PhD in 1993 and has since advised 35 PhD students, 17 postdocs, and hundreds of undergraduate students. He has a personal interest in proving that half of the partition numbers are even or that Ramanujan's tau function never vanishes. His father taught him as a boy about Ramanujan, who believed a Hindu goddess gave him mathematical formulas in his dreams. The Navier-Stokes equations model how fluids swirl and eddy, and the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a one million dollar prize for them. OpenAI denied allegations of foul play regarding the Navier-Stokes proof, and reports suggest they took a different route than Buckmaster.

Universities, funding agencies, journals, and employers must now decide what they support and reward as AI continues to solve centuries-old mathematical problems. Ken Ono will argue that students and mathematicians who choose to work without AI should have a voice in these decisions. He intends to ask his students what they originated and ensure readers know who contributed ideas in the work he publishes. Buckmaster and Alpöge have not yet released the certificate for their latest result, though they claimed it would be released soon. The articles leave open how the mathematical community will handle attribution and whether young mathematicians can still find rewarding careers.

stories.Headline: Lagarde calls AI-boosted cyber threat her top worry for finance
stories.Summary:
European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said on Friday that the greatest immediate challenge facing the world of finance may be cyber threats supercharged by increasingly sophisticated AI agents. She made the remark at the European Banking Congress in Frankfurt, where she told the audience that this combination of AI and cyber threat is the one that keeps her awake. Lagarde added that many others in the room share that worry as well. She said policymakers have not paid enough attention to this threat.

Lagarde said attackers are often anonymous and difficult to track, and they rely on dubious funding that often comes from toxic states with a vested interest in disrupting the world. Her remarks were reported by CNA on Friday, November 20, 2026, in a story datelined Frankfurt. The report carried a file photo illustration taken on October 22, 2026, showing the words AI Hacking and PHP code on a screen. The article gave no further figures, dates or names beyond Lagarde, the congress and the ECB.

Lagarde is the president of the European Central Bank, and she used her speech at the congress to name AI applied together with cyber threat as her top worry. She said the threat deserves more attention from policymakers than it has received so far. The articles do not say what measures, if any, the ECB or other authorities plan to take in response. They also do not say what happens next.

stories.Headline: Coatue Management discloses a stake in SK hynix as HBM chip demand accelerates
stories.Summary:
Coatue Management disclosed a stake in SK hynix, the South Korean memory chip maker whose high-bandwidth memory products are used in artificial intelligence hardware, according to a TradingView report dated November 20, 2026. The report tied the position to accelerating demand for HBM chips, the specialized memory that has driven the company's recent results. The same article recorded that SK hynix shares fell 5.92% to 1,113,000 won at the November 20 regular-session close in Seoul, as fears about AI spending swept Asian chip stocks. The Kospi fell 5.21% that day, its steepest slide in months, after Nvidia and AMD sank on Wall Street overnight.

The article said the fundamentals look nothing like a crash, with third-quarter revenue reaching 104.6 trillion won, up 328% year over year, and operating profit hitting 83.3 trillion won, an 80% margin. SK hynix holds 98.7 trillion won of net cash, and long-term agreements with 14 major customers cover more than half of 2027 and 2028 capacity, while management expects demand to exceed supply through 2030. Shareholder returns for 2026 total about 100 trillion won, including a 20 trillion won buyback approved with the results. GuruFocus gives the stock a GF Score of 99/100 and a GF Value of 1,517,314 won, putting the close at a 26.6% discount that it rates modestly undervalued.

The article attributed the nervousness to valuation rather than operations, noting that net cash covers about 12% of the 813 trillion won market value and that the market cap is only about 2.4 times last quarter's annualized operating profit, a cycle-peak multiple. It said the test is whether HBM4 shipments overtake HBM3E in the fourth quarter as guided, which is the company's own forecast rather than an outside estimate. The report did not give the size of the Coatue position, the date it was taken or any comment from Coatue or SK hynix management on the investment. It also did not say what happens next beyond the fourth-quarter shipment test and the demand outlook management expects to hold through 2030.

stories.Headline: Microsoft powers a race machine for the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team to improve performance
stories.Summary:
Toto Wolff and Judson Althoff spoke with Yahoo Finance on November 20, 2026, about artificial intelligence at Mercedes. Microsoft now powers a race machine for the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team to help them win races. This partnership integrates compute intensive AI across various parts of the professional motorsport operation to improve their overall performance. The team uses these tools for car design, factory workflows, personnel management, and race day strategy during events. They specifically applied these rapid calculations during the Singapore Grand Prix to help driver Kimi make a passing move.

The system runs more than 10 million race day simulations to provide data for the engineers and the driver. Althoff described a layered infrastructure involving analysts in the United Kingdom, engineers in the pit garage, and the cockpit. Microsoft also rents AI computing power from CoreWeave, which saw sales to other customers rise by about 700 million dollars. Microsoft canceled a 3.22 billion dollar order for an Nscale data center in Essex, England, due to grid connection delays. This specific site connection was expected to slip into the 2030s, leading to the cancellation of the planned project.

Toto Wolff acts as a mediator between the data driven engineering culture and the instinct driven world of the driver. He stated that he sides with the human because the driver must feel confidence while driving the car. Wolff believes the person behind the wheel is the most expensive instrument and the most valuable sensor the team deploys. Judson Althoff noted that people outside the sport would struggle to appreciate the sheer pressure and intensity of compute. Satya Nadella told Jim Cramer that selling AI capacity to only one or two customers is not a business.

Driver preference overrides what the numbers identify as the faster setup because the human must operate under extreme conditions. CoreWeave serves other customers like Nissan and the Aston Martin Formula 1 team to help them speed up engineering tests. Nscale received 52 percent of its first half revenue from one unnamed customer and has deals with Anthropic for power. OpenAI accounted for about 45 percent of 625 billion dollars in contracted commercial sales that Microsoft had not yet recorded. This commercial backlog for Microsoft reached 677 billion dollars by September, though the share for OpenAI was not disclosed.

The friction between sensor records and physical feelings predates the current wave of AI and remains a persistent team tension. Microsoft builds for the long term by leasing and renting power when they run short of their own computing capacity. The company owns a stake in OpenAI worth around 136 billion dollars and has proprietary IP of models until 2030. Microsoft uses Azure to rent out AI power and runs paid products such as the Microsoft 365 Copilot for users. Satya Nadella explained that the company lines up land and power early because data centers take time to build.

Microsoft can shift capacity between Azure and paid products as demand changes to maximize the use of their AI chips. Nscale has not locked in financing for computing power that could make its August deals with Anthropic worth 44.6 billion. Investors are questioning how much of the commercial backlog comes from the broader customer base that Nadella wants to serve. It remains open whether Microsoft can build a viable general purpose frontier model to catch up with OpenAI and Anthropic. The company may use its enterprise data moat and OpenAI blueprints to create its own intelligent AI models eventually.

stories.Headline: Samsung appoints HBM and Galaxy veterans to lead memory and mobile divisions
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics carried out its regular executive appointments for 2027 on Friday, November 20, 2026, to build a management structure centered on technological leadership. The company named Hwang Sang-joon as the new head of the memory division and Choi Won-joon as the head of the MX division. Hwang previously spearheaded the mass production of HBM4, while Choi is a veteran of Galaxy development with twenty six years of experience. These leadership changes allow the two co-CEOs to focus more on the robotics and foundry businesses. The reorganization aims to leverage technical talent to maintain a competitive edge against rivals in the semiconductor and mobile markets.

Hwang must direct the development race for HBM4E and HBM5 to overtake rivals next year after market share reached the high thirty percent range. Choi will lead the MX division, which posted losses for two straight quarters, toward a turnaround using new foldable products and AI glasses. The first AI glasses, called Intelligent Eyewear, will launch on December 10, and the Galaxy Z TriFold2 is due for release next year. Vice Chairman Jun Young-hyun remains head of the DS division, while President Roh Tae-moon retains his post as head of the DX division. This two-track structure oversees a turn to profit in foundry and the new physical AI business involving humanoid robots.

Hwang Sang-joon is responsible for the memory division and is tasked with securing a lead in the next generation of high bandwidth memory. Choi Won-joon is responsible for the MX division and seeks an earnings rebound as Chinese rivals struggle in the mobile market. Vice Chairman Jun Young-hyun continues to manage the DS division to ensure the company returns to profitability within its foundry operations. President Roh Tae-moon remains in charge of the DX division to oversee the development of the company's new humanoid robot business. These executives are expected to drive the company's technical momentum forward through their respective specialized divisions of memory and mobile devices.

Rival executives are advised to closely monitor this reorganization because Samsung is shifting its leadership focus toward high level technical talent. The MX division is particularly affected by two consecutive quarters of losses, making the success of new AI products critical for recovery. Consumers will be affected by the upcoming release of the Galaxy Z TriFold2 and the Intelligent Eyewear glasses starting in December. The memory division is reacting to a previous plunge in HBM3E market share, which had fallen to around twenty percent during competition. These changes target a recovery in market share and a return to profitability across both the semiconductor and mobile hardware sectors.

The company's HBM market share recovered to the high thirty percent range in the third quarter after securing an early lead in HBM4. Samsung previously struggled during the HBM3E competition, but the appointment of Hwang reflects a strategy to prioritize those who led mass production. The MX division has faced financial difficulties recently, resulting in losses for two straight quarters before these new executive appointments were made. The company is now positioning itself to compete with Chinese rivals who are currently struggling in the global mobile phone market. This background shows a shift toward technical expertise to reverse losses and capitalize on the growing demand for AI memory.

Samsung will now focus on the HBM4E and HBM5 development race with the goal of overtaking its competitors by next year. The company will launch its Intelligent Eyewear on December 10 and release the Galaxy Z TriFold2 during the following calendar year. The DS division will continue working toward a turn to profit in foundry, while the DX division develops physical AI. The articles leave open whether the MX division can successfully end its sales slide and achieve a full earnings rebound. It remains unclear if the new leadership can maintain the high thirty percent market share in the face of intense competition.

stories.Headline: Trump urges Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to apologize and warns of taxes on overseas data centers
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump told reporters on November 20 that he would like to see Nvidia chief Jensen Huang receive a second chance. Trump described Huang as one of the smartest people in the world and a good man who made some bad choices. The president expressed hope that Huang would apologize in a big way and return after creating the advanced Blackwell chip. Trump also mentioned that Chinese President Xi Jinping called Huang a brilliant man during their meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.

Trump warned on Thursday that the United States will charge a tremendous tax on companies that build data centers in other countries. This stance follows the Senate's passage of the Bipartisan American Cost of Living Relief and Jobs Act on November 19. This pending bill would require large data centers to pay for their own power demand instead of passing those costs to small businesses or households. The legislation must still clear the House of Representatives before it can officially take effect.

Trump stated that the United States must compete fiercely to ensure that China does not take over the data center market. He argued that the country fell behind in semiconductors because plants were built abroad and insisted that new facilities must be built at home. Regarding espionage allegations involving Alice Huang, Trump suggested that nobody can be certain of the facts and noted that the U.S. also conducts intelligence activities against China. He urged that companies should pay money into the community but should not be blocked from operating.

stories.Headline: Anthropic shares fall 9.1% as AI trade selloff hits global markets
stories.Summary:
Shares in Anthropic plunged 9.1 per cent on Friday, November 20, 2026, as a broad selloff hit Asia and the United States. The company behind the Claude chatbot saw its stock price drop almost to the initial public offering price during the day. Trading eventually closed at US$88.30 per share after the company pared some of its losses. This decline followed a first day jump on Thursday that had previously boosted the company's valuation. The event occurred as the wider artificial intelligence and technology trade began to unravel across global markets.

The listing gave Anthropic a market value of about US$1.6 trillion, ranking it among the fifteen biggest publicly traded companies. The company raised US$119.5 billion total, including US$93.5 billion from the IPO and US$26 billion from a private placement. Underwriting banks, including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, exercised a greenshoe over-allotment option to sell additional shares to the public. These twenty-two banks earned a record US$550 million in fees, with the two lead firms collecting about US$113 million each. The offering pushed the combined wealth of the seven founders to US$166 billion.

Emmanuel Valavanis of Forte Securities said there is a buyers strike for Anthropic and the wider artificial intelligence and tech trade. He noted that many clients without allocations are not prepared to pick up the pieces from the market hangover. Raphael Thuin of Tikehau Capital said he was impressed by the wealth creation and the company's reasonable cash flow burn. However, Thuin added that he would prefer more diversified businesses and wants post IPO volatility to fade before engaging. Ravi Mhatre of Lightspeed Venture Partners said the public listing shows there is a viable business model.

The selloff affected the Nasdaq 100 Index, which fell 5.6 per cent, and the S&P 500 Index, which sank 3.7 per cent. Ann Miletti of Allspring Global Investments said demand was positive, but investors still worry about the actual returns of AI. Fund manager Olivier David of Vega IS stated he would consider buying if the stock gets close to the IPO price. The volatility index spiked to over 29, a level where companies typically do not find the market welcoming for IPOs. Employees were able to sell holdings immediately, with some 2024 options potentially worth US$66 million.

Anthropic is the first frontier AI model maker to go public and its IPO eclipsed the June SpaceX record of US$86.2 billion. The company has more than 11,900 customers delivering US$100,000 of revenue each on a trailing twelve month basis as of September. Its run-rate revenue reached US$81 billion by October 31, which was US$10 billion higher than at the end of September. The company's coding agent, Claude Code, is used by software developers and engineers at Nasa. First time stock sales raised US$258 billion this year, beating the US$195 billion haul seen in 2021.

Investors are now testing whether there is an appetite for companies pioneering AI technology rather than those making chips and data centres. The market is waiting to see if the current volatility fades and if the stock price drops below the IPO level. This debut sets the stage for rival OpenAI, which does not plan to go public before the year 2027. Spark Capital holds a stake valued at US$17.1 billion after investing US$75 million in the company during 2023. The articles leave open whether the AI trade can revive or if investors will remain on the sidelines.

stories.Headline: Optima Arch's AI-made Slotbound sells 100,000 copies in three days on Steam
stories.Summary:
On November 13, 2026, the indie game Slotbound launched on Steam and sold 100,000 copies within three days, according to eu.36kr.com. South Korean individual developer Optima Arch made the game, which combines 3×3 slot machine gameplay with Roguelike and auto-battle mechanisms. Sales revenue reached 356,000 US dollars in the first 48 hours, and sales exceeded 50,000 copies in that same period. The game's peak concurrent player count exceeded 30,000. By contrast, other AI-made games drew almost no attention one month after release, with some earning less than 10 US dollars.

Mobilegamer.biz interviewed multiple individual developers who used AI tools to make games, asking about actual download volumes and revenues. Ahmed Alshuail's Sprout: Cozy Idle Garden landed on Google Play on August 30, 2026, and on the App Store on September 30. As of October 28, it had 121 downloads and about 6 US dollars in revenue, with 4 US dollars from IAP and about 2 US dollars from advertising. Marc Fienberg's Zen Ten Match, built with Claude Code, React Native and Supabase plus RevenueCat and AdMob, had 74 real players across iOS, Android and web as of October 13, with about 3 US dollars in advertising revenue in its first three weeks. Arin Agrawal's Calc Quest, made with Flutter, accumulated more than 25,000 players but only about 120 US dollars from advertising and IAP.

Iain Atkinson's Tennis Tycoon, made with Claude, sold about 3,000 US dollars, but AI Tokens during development cost thousands of US dollars. Ivan Soyer, developer of Dusk Climber, said he invested about 1,500 US dollars in AI tools and Tokens, and the game got about 1,000 downloads one month after launch but has not generated any revenue yet. Optima Arch said that in 2025, introduced by his family, he first came into contact with AI game development. He did not even know how to get started, so he first asked AI to make a square that can move via WASD keys. When that simple program ran successfully, he gradually began to try to make a complete game.

Before the official launch, Optima Arch had released the Demo on itch.io and Steam and continuously shared development progress on social platforms. In September 2026, the number of Steam wishlists for Slotbound had exceeded 100,000. Deniz Sancar's 38-0-0, a football draft game made with Claude Code, topped the free game list on iOS in the UK in the summer of 2026. It has accumulated about 300,000 downloads on iOS and more than 700,000 on Android, and Sancar said revenue from advertising and IAP is enough to support full-time game development. Ken Law's Harpagia, a text-based idle RPG for iOS and Android, has accumulated about 155,000 US dollars in revenue over the past year, averaging about 13,000 US dollars a month, with total downloads above 50,000.

Ken Law previously worked in technical roles at Amazon and Meta, with about 12 years of experience in the technology industry. After getting in touch with AI tools, he began to try to use Cursor and ChatGPT to assist in game development. According to an interview with Starter Story in September 2026, Harpagia has not launched paid advertising campaigns and mainly acquires users through organic traffic, with daily operating costs of about 500 US dollars per month. Law has an educational background in computer science and has long been engaged in software engineering and technical management work. Sancar has a background in the marketing industry, and his own marketing company runs alongside his game work.

The articles leave open the specific revenue of 38-0-0, which the developer has not announced. They leave open how Slotbound's sales and revenue developed after the third day and after the first 48 hours. They leave open whether the developers whose games earned little will change their products or marketing. They leave open what share of the games' downloads or revenue came from AI-assisted work versus other factors. They leave open how the interviewed developers' figures were verified.

stories.Headline: OpenAI and Google expand advertising in AI interfaces to target high-intent users
stories.Summary:
OpenAI and Google are rapidly expanding advertising inside their artificial intelligence interfaces, which gives marketers new ways to target users who show high purchasing intent, Axios reported on November 21, 2026. The report, written by Sara Fischer, said user intent is much higher with AI interfaces than with traditional search because conversations let consumers reveal their needs with far more specificity. The story drew on data from Similarweb and Graphite, with a chart by Christine Wang of Axios. The article described the shift as an attention crunch for AI advertising. The change means marketers can aim at people whose conversations already signal what they want to buy, rather than at people typing short queries into a search box.

The article gave no figures beyond the two data sources, Similarweb and Graphite, and named no dollar amounts, user counts or dates other than the November 21, 2026 publication. It said the higher intent comes from the back and forth of a conversation, which lets a consumer state a need more precisely than a search query usually does. Both OpenAI and Google are named as the companies expanding ads in their AI products. The article attributed the reporting to Sara Fischer and presented the data through Similarweb and Graphite, with the chart credited to Christine Wang of Axios. It did not include direct statements from OpenAI, Google or any marketer, so no executive comments were reported.

The piece framed the higher intent of AI conversations as the reason the ad expansion matters to advertisers. It did not say how the ads are priced, sold or displayed. The context the article gives is a comparison between AI interfaces and traditional search, with conversations producing stronger signals of what a consumer wants. It did not say what happens next, beyond noting that both companies are rapidly expanding the ads. No timeline, revenue target or response from either company appeared in the text.

stories.Headline: Anthropic executive Aiden Blake helps drive record $81 billion stock market launch
stories.Summary:
Aiden Blake, a Letterkenny man who is Anthropic's Head of Startup Sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, is set to profit from the company's stock market launch, according to Donegal Daily. The ex long-time Google executive has worked with the AI startup since November of 2025, and as one of its most senior employees in the Dublin office he is likely to be one of its biggest beneficiaries from the floatation. Anthropic's arrival on the stock market raised $81 billion and its stock price landed at $97 a share by closing on opening day, the article says, though the price dipped to $85 by closing on Friday. The company offered €8.4 million in share-based remuneration to its employees in 2025, but no specifics relating to a guaranteed sale price in the event of a public offering were included in its public filings. Aiden is married to Ballybofey native Rachel Heeney, a long-time Google employee herself, and his father is Laurence Blake, a prominent Letterkenny businessman, while his mum Denise Blake is a well-known poet and writer.

Axios reports that with its IPO done, Anthropic's shareholders will be watching its progress toward becoming a business that does not need constant capital infusions from investors and vendors. Anthropic, along with OpenAI, sits at the heart of the industry that has dominated the equity and debt markets for the last four years, and much of the AI infrastructure boom is ultimately aimed at supplying computing power to these two companies. The bill for that data center investment will start to come due over the next few years, and Anthropic and OpenAI are going to have to pay for quite a bit of it. Anthropic has covered much of its computing costs so far by selling parts of itself to compute vendors like Amazon and Alphabet and by raising more cash from other investors, but eventually its core business will have to generate enough money to cover those costs on its own.

Anthropic's filings say it is on the hook for roughly $900 billion in spending commitments, mostly for data centers and computing power, with about half of that due before the end of 2030, according to Axios. After the IPO the company is expected to have roughly $200 billion in cash and short-term investments in the bank, which should buy it some time, but its sales will have to be a lot higher to just cover computing obligations, let alone the profits its new shareholders are expecting. Anthropic posted a loss of roughly $23 billion on revenue of nearly $17 billion in the third quarter, and much of that loss stems from a non-cash accounting charge of almost $22 billion. Even operating income, which strips out paper losses and gains, still shows an operating loss of more than half a billion dollars in the third quarter, and the article concludes that Anthropic still has a long way to go before it is standing on its own feet financially.
