stories.Headline: Singapore and Future of Finance Institute launch AI initiatives for financial services
stories.Summary:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Future of Finance Institute launched several AI initiatives for financial services in November 2026. These programs were unveiled during the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 to accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence across the sector. The initiatives focus on improving business financing, preventing fraud, and ensuring the safe use of autonomous AI agents. They support the National AI Missions for financial services by providing data and enabling controlled testing of AI transactions. These efforts follow national AI priorities outlined by Deputy Prime Minister and MAS Chairman Gan Kim Yong.

The AI Innovation Arena provides synthetic datasets to developers and research institutions to build solutions for financial crime and scam detection. MAS will provide a synthetic dataset reflecting interbank transaction patterns and scam activities pooled from five participating banks. The Agentic Money Sandbox allows financial institutions to experiment with AI agents that initiate transactions using digital money under predefined limits. FFI will work with A*STAR’s Institute of Advanced Intelligence and Computing to advance locally developed speech-to-text technology into live pilots. MAS will begin a design study in early 2027 for an industry-wide Scam Detection Utility focusing on domestic accounts.

Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong stated that the programs bring banks, researchers, and public agencies together to develop shared AI capabilities. He explained that scam proceeds move through institutions quickly, making it difficult for any single lender to recognize the full sequence. Gan noted that AI could help lenders assess a wider set of indicators to speed up decisions for small businesses. He stressed that greater autonomy for AI agents would not remove responsibility from the organisations that authorize those agents. The Future of Finance Institute will coordinate work to develop common standards and resources for managing various AI risks.

Technology companies are invited to develop lending tools using synthetic data to help start-ups that lack extensive financial histories or assets. Participating businesses will be consulted to see if the proposed AI tools effectively address their specific financing and borrowing difficulties. Financial institutions including DBS, OCBC, Standard Chartered, and UOB are named as the launch partners for the new institute. The initiatives affect developers and technology companies who can now use pooled data to train and evaluate machine learning models. The government intends to explore if AI can help lenders proactively identify businesses that are approaching a financing need.

The initiatives form part of a wider national AI programme that was announced in the Singapore 2026 Budget. The synthetic dataset for scam detection was developed with the Government Technology Agency of Singapore to improve machine learning models. FFI will partner with AI Singapore to develop financial sector talent through apprenticeship programmes and a wider industry network. The government is currently engaging American officials regarding the implications of new United States export controls on advanced computing equipment. These efforts reflect a move beyond experimentation toward the practical deployment of AI while addressing security and governance requirements.

Authorities will assess promising applications against international practices before considering broader deployment as the work moves into the trial phase. The government will not assume that successful demonstrations automatically translate into reliable commercial systems for the wider financial services industry. Future cooperation may expand to cross-border scam detection after the initial focus on domestic accounts and information is completed. The articles leave open whether the proposed AI lending assessments will successfully lower borrowing costs for small and medium enterprises. It remains unclear how the government will resolve the uncertainty regarding access to advanced computing equipment under US export controls.

stories.Headline: US regulators scrutinize Nscale for providing ByteDance access to Nvidia GPUs
stories.Summary:
The US Bureau of Industry and Security is scrutinizing the London based cloud provider Nscale for its compute agreements. This regulatory examination began after a Commerce Department rule took effect on November 19, 2026, to restrict advanced chips. Nscale provided remote access to high performance graphics processing units to a subsidiary of the Chinese conglomerate ByteDance. The company leased these chips to Spring (SG) Pte. Ltd., which is a wholly owned Singaporean unit of ByteDance.

This arrangement allowed a China headquartered entity to access state of the art computational capacity through an offshore model. The rule requires a US license for data centers providing over 12 million units of total processing performance to restricted parties. Nscale leased 2,304 Nvidia B200 Blackwell GPUs at its Glomfjord, Norway site, which is powered by regional hydroelectric generation. The company must obtain this license within a 90 day window ending in mid February 2027 to avoid enforcement. This requirement applies to data centers in countries including Norway and Iceland under the Federal Register publication 91 FR 74970.

The specific hardware is subject to ECCN 3A090 controls and the new Section 744.24 of the Export Administration Regulations. The US Department of Commerce is responsible for this rule, which aims to stop Chinese companies from reaching advanced AI chips. Officials stated the rule addresses remote access to advanced semiconductors to close a loophole used by foreign infrastructure providers. Nscale warned in its November 12 IPO filing that US authorities could interpret existing regulations aggressively to restrict its services. The company has not yet stated whether it will apply for the required license to keep its biggest customer.

There is currently no indication from the government regarding whether such a license would be granted to the firm. Institutional investors and semiconductor analysts have responded with caution, revising Nscale's valuation target from $30 billion down to $16 billion or $19 billion. The rule affects university research teams and high performance computing consortia that rely on distributed cloud environments for large scale simulations. Research offices must now implement screening protocols to verify the parentage of collaborators to avoid federal grant debarment or sanctions.

Banks also reacted to the situation, with reports that some paused a $480 million chip loan tied to ByteDance. The outcome of this case will establish a benchmark for how the US polices international cloud compute hubs. In 2025, the contract with Spring generated about $24 million, which was 73 percent of Nscale's $33 million total annual revenue. For the first half of 2026, this customer accounted for 52 percent of the company's $140.6 million in revenue.

Nscale used a $105 million Macquarie Bank facility to finance the Glomfjord cluster, with Spring's cash flows collateralizing the debt. To reduce this dependence, Nscale signed infrastructure agreements with enterprise AI leaders including Microsoft and the company Anthropic. The company also has statements of work with Microsoft worth up to $43.8 billion through December 2033. Nscale must now decide if it will submit a formal license application before the mid February 2027 deadline.

A 60 day public comment period on the technical thresholds of the rule runs through January 19, 2027. The industry is waiting to see if the government adopts a policy of presumptive denial for all Chinese affiliated entities. It remains open whether verifiable cryptographic isolation and strict screening can enable continued multi tenant operations for these cloud providers. The articles leave it unclear if Nscale will successfully dilute its revenue dependence on Chinese entities before facing potential shortfalls.

stories.Headline: Modi inaugurates IIT Patna AI centre and lays research park foundation
stories.Summary:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi virtually inaugurated the AI Centre of Excellence at IIT Patna on November 21. He also laid foundation stones for a research park and a startup hostel. A. Prathibha inaugurated the NIELIT transit campus in Guntur on Saturday. This new facility is India's first AI and Quantum University campus. It is located at the Centre for Distance Education building of Acharya Nagarjuna University.

The IIT Patna research park costs 400 crore rupees, with 305 crore from Bihar and 95 crore from HEFA. The AI Centre of Excellence requires 60 crore rupees and operates as a Section 8 non-profit company. A 120-bed hostel will house startup incubatees at IIT Patna. The NIELIT campus in Guntur will start training programmes on December 1, 2026. It is situated on the premises of Acharya Nagarjuna University in Guntur district.

The Prime Minister's Office stated these projects will strengthen research, innovation, and entrepreneurship in Bihar. A. Prathibha said NIELIT will promote advanced education and research in quantum computing and VLSI design. NIELIT Director General Dr. Madan Mohan Tripathi called the Amaravati centre a milestone for skilled human resources. Bhaskar Katamneni promised 100 per cent support from the Andhra Pradesh government. C.V. Sridhar noted that students can use quantum testbeds at Medha Towers and SRM University.

The research park will support researchers, startups, and micro, small and medium enterprises. The startup hostel provides entrepreneurs with access to laboratories and guidance from faculty members. Students at the NIELIT campus will gain opportunities for advanced training in specialised technology fields. The AI Centre is supported by Tiger Analytics, the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, and Bihar. S. Vijaya Bhaskara Rao and K. Gangadhara Rao also participated in the Guntur inauguration programme.

The AI Centre of Excellence at IIT Patna is led by the institute as its academic partner. The NIELIT transit campus is an autonomous scientific society under the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. NIELIT already has an existing campus in Tirupati that focuses on semiconductor research. The Guntur facility aims to strengthen the technical education ecosystem through state-of-the-art laboratory facilities. The research park provides facilities for designing, developing, testing prototypes, fabrication, manufacturing, and product certification.

NIELIT courses will cover quantum communication, chip design, embedded systems, and the Internet of Things. Short-term courses will include automotive electronics, battery management, system information security, and semiconductor packaging. The projects aim to help researchers and startups turn their ideas into actual products. The articles do not state when the IIT Patna research park and hostel will be completed. They also leave open the specific dates for the short-term course offerings at the NIELIT campus.

stories.Headline: Thinking Machines Lab releases Inkling 2 Mini local AI model
stories.Summary:
Thinking Machines Lab released the Inkling 2 Mini local AI model on November 20, 2026. This new multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model uses a looped transformer architecture to increase its capacity. It features approximately 26 billion physical total parameters and 3 billion active parameters per token. The model accepts both text and image inputs and supports a 1 million-token context size. It is designed specifically for local AI setups and is smaller than Inkling 2 Small.

The model uses 24 physical decoder layers, but 12 middle layers run three times in a loop. This process makes the model act as if it had 48 logical layers. It uses NVFP4 and MXFP8 expert weights in a mixed-precision format and includes a DSpark drafter. The router selects eight of 128 SwiGLU experts for each token at every layer visit. The hidden size is 2,304, and the intermediate width of each expert is 1,152.

Thinking Machines Lab stated that they believe this is a refreshingly new great local model. They noted that the model is at least comparable with Qwen 3.8 27B in vibe tests. The developers mentioned that more validation is needed for the model. They also released a research artifact that allows for a variable number of loop passes. They observed that using one or two passes makes inference faster but may lower quality.

The model leads in 32 out of 48 benchmarks in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5. These benchmarks cover reasoning, knowledge, safety, alignment, vision interpretation, creation, coding, autoresearch, agentic search, and tool use. It outperforms Gemma 4 31B, Muse Glimmer, Qwen3.8-27B, and Nemotron 3.5 Super VL in these categories. It leads in FrontierCode v2.0 and ties with Qwen3.8-27B on Terminal-Bench 4.0. However, it trails Qwen on AutomationBench-AA v1.0.6.

The model uses a looped core where every pass starts from the output of the first six layers. Information moves between these passes through cross-pass messages using learned queries. A gating controller decides how much of the current input to forget and how much message to add. Each six-layer block contains five sliding-window layers and one full-attention layer. The local window for these layers holds up to 1,024 tokens.

The model is available for use in transformers, llama.cpp, MLX, and SGLang. GGUF 4-bit and 8-bit quants are provided for the Llama App on macOS and Windows. Users can set reasoning effort levels from none to max using numeric values from 0.0 to 0.99. SGLang provides day-zero inference support for production deployments on datacenter hardware. The articles do not state if further versions of the Inkling series will be released.

stories.Headline: Vinit Goenka warns in Nagpur that every click leaves a trace and urges India to keep critical data within its borders
stories.Summary:
Vinit Goenka flagged a threat to data privacy during a session in Nagpur on November 23, 2026. He spoke at an event titled Who Controls Your Data to discuss the risks of digital tracking. Goenka serves as the secretary of the Centre for Knowledge Sovereignty and addressed the current economy. He highlighted how every click leaves a trace that can be used to monitor various users. The session included a conversation with Kartik Borikar, who is the MD of KKE Wash Systems.

Goenka stated that critical information should remain within India's borders to ensure greater data sovereignty for the nation. He noted that personal data from search engines, social media platforms, mobile phones, and digital payment services is risky. This information can be used to influence national interests and the interests of individuals according to the speaker. He claimed that mobile networks and online searches can track users even when location services are switched off. Goenka also cautioned against using sensors, facial recognition systems, and CCTV cameras for surveillance purposes.

Vinit Goenka said that data has become the biggest weapon in the economy of today for those controlling it. He explained that the perspectives of those who control AI data can shape public narratives and influence responses. The speaker claimed that the war has entered the house and is now present at the dinner table. He urged the youth of India to develop their own technology platforms within the borders of the country. Goenka advised people to be careful online and urged them not to share unnecessary personal information or OTPs.

The articles do not mention other people who spoke during the session or specific groups that were affected. However, the text notes that the perspectives of those controlling AI data can influence the general public narratives. The speaker suggested that individual and national interests are at risk when personal data is collected by digital platforms. He warned that surveillance technologies like facial recognition and sensors could be misused to track people without their knowledge. Users of mobile phones and digital payment services are the ones whose data is being collected and used.

The provided text explains that data is collected through various digital services and mobile networks to track user behavior. It notes that AI data can be used to shape narratives and that surveillance technology is becoming more common. The articles mention that location services are not the only way that mobile networks can track a user's movements. There is a focus on the need for data sovereignty to keep critical information within the borders of India. The background provided emphasizes that digital traces are left by almost every action taken by a user online.

Goenka encouraged the youth to create technology platforms in India to reduce the reliance on foreign data control systems. He advised users to avoid sharing OTPs and other personal details to protect themselves from potential online risks. The articles do not state what specific laws or policies will be changed following these warnings about data privacy. It remains open whether the Indian government will implement new rules to keep critical information within the national borders. The text does not explain how the youth will be supported in developing these new domestic technology platforms.

stories.Headline: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress defends AI spending as shares fall 14%
stories.Summary:
Nvidia shares fell more than 14% in Friday's regular trading on November 20, 2026, their worst single-day fall in about 22 months, before gaining nearly 4% in the afterhours session. The drop came amid concerns that the AI boom is running out of steam, with slowing growth expectations, margin pressure and questions over hyperscaler spending weighing on investor sentiment. Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue for the three months ending October 25, more than double the $57 billion of the year prior and above analysts' expectations of $109 billion. It was Nvidia's first earnings report without Jensen Huang as CEO, posted late Tuesday, November 17, 2026. NVDA stock is down 33% year-to-date, while the S&P 500 ETF is up 6% and the Invesco QQQ Trust is up 4% over the past 12 months.

Nvidia spent $58.1 billion buying other companies' stock in the nine months ending October 25, nearly 12 times the $4.95 billion it spent in the same period last year. That almost matches the $61.2 billion Nvidia spent on stock buybacks, up from $36.3 billion last year. Nvidia's equity investments are focused on frontier labs, infrastructure financiers and other private companies, according to its Q3 2026 CFO commentary, and Nvidia has invested in OpenAI and Anthropic. Nvidia's future commitments to neoclouds totaled $32 billion in Q3, and its total credit guarantees reached $118 billion, including $105 billion in credit support for the PORTS-Pike data center project in Ohio, which will host Nvidia infrastructure under a 20-year lease with OpenAI. Nvidia has $227.3 billion left under its stock buyback authorization program, which Kress said it intends to use by the end of fiscal 2028.

Interim CEO Colette Kress told analysts on the November 17 earnings call that giving returns to shareholders is a "super top priority." She said another priority is supporting Nvidia's suppliers who "are working feverishly to build more" and might need "assistance in terms of capital," adding "we want to make sure that we're there for them." Kress said Nvidia is willing to help finance select customers' data centers but called it "a lot of work to understand if those are the right types of investments." She said some guarantees only take effect once customers get financing for their data centers and may no longer apply if construction runs into trouble, noting "our guarantee for most of these are really about when they are ready to go." Kress said cloud industry backlog now sits at $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion just three months ago, underscoring the significant multi-year opportunity ahead of Nvidia's partners and of Nvidia.

James Kisner, managing director of technology at Water Tower Research, told Fortune that if AI spending falters Nvidia could suffer from both lower chip sales and falling valuations of the companies it has invested in, saying "it's magnified and you feel more pain because you're kind of double exposed here." Kisner said Nvidia's billions in free cash flow mean it can afford the $58.1 billion in outside stock but that can be seen as fueling its own demand, and that "if you were really cynical, you could say, 'Oh, like these guys are just generating their own demand.'" He said there are "all kinds of incentives for them to fuel the fire if they have the cash, so there's a self-serving aspect," and that the markets really reward them for pouring all this money. Kisner said the strategy reflects Huang's approach of "spreading money around and kind of keeping the ecosystem going," and he sees Kress continuing it with "a little more conservatism" at the margins. Equity securities only generated $1.8 billion in net gains for Nvidia in Q3, which included a $1 billion loss from non-marketable equity securities.

IO Fund's Beth Kindig argued that investors may be mistaking a temporary pause for a fundamental slowdown, pointing to Nvidia's latest results, expanding AI demand and a valuation that has fallen sharply even as growth expectations remain elevated. Nvidia's transition to its Vera Rubin platform appears to be progressing faster than its previous Blackwell ramp, according to Kindig, with Rubin generating approximately $20 billion in revenue in its first quarter of production shipments, nearly double Blackwell's $11 billion in its initial quarter. Kindig pointed to Nvidia's fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook, which implies growth of approximately 75%, up from 70% projected for fiscal 2027 despite a larger revenue base. She highlighted that Nvidia's supply-related commitments surged to $390 billion in Q3 of fiscal 2027, up from $119 billion just two quarters earlier, and pointed to SK Hynix's comments about being effectively sold out through 2029. Nvidia reported that token prices have fallen nearly 60% since May while token consumption has accelerated, and Kindig cited Hopper GPUs being recontracted at up to twice their original prices under multiyear agreements and B300 rental rates rising more than 60% since introduction.

Nvidia became the first company to cross the $5 trillion market valuation mark last year, though it has since dropped to $3.7 trillion as of November 18, per Yahoo Finance data. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Nvidia trended in the "extremely bullish" territory at the time of writing. During the Blackwell ramp, sequential revenue growth slowed before accelerating again as demand picked up, and Kindig suggested the current transition could follow a similar pattern, with temporary growth moderation mistaken for longer-term deterioration in demand. Kindig sees the decline in AI token prices as an example of "Jevons Paradox," where improvements in efficiency and lower costs can ultimately lead to greater consumption, and argues AI workloads are increasingly spreading across different GPU generations rather than being concentrated exclusively on the newest hardware. Kress said "all of this is creating a powerful flywheel," and Kindig believes that is another sign that AI demand remains robust rather than showing signs of saturation.

stories.Headline: Danaher partners with Microsoft to develop AI powered scientific instruments
stories.Summary:
Danaher announced a strategic partnership with Microsoft on November 20, 2026, to develop smart scientific instruments. The companies will build an interoperable agentic ecosystem and cloud based software to accelerate scientific experiments. This collaboration aims to streamline lab execution by pairing instrumentation expertise with artificial intelligence capabilities. Early tools are already moving toward commercial rollout to help researchers turn questions into evidence faster. The partnership focuses on creating a shared agentic platform for instrument control and insight generation.

The platform uses Microsoft Azure for secure cloud infrastructure and Microsoft Foundry to power the AI agents. Danaher will deliver first commercial applications this year, including the MetaXpress Acquire AI Assistant from Molecular Devices. Next generation agent enabled instruments are planned for 2027 to assist scientists across four core laboratory functions. These functions include translating scientific intent, controlling hardware, interpreting results, and recommending corrective actions for human review. The system remains open to external agents and digital tools across multi vendor laboratories.

Danaher aims to embed its hardware more deeply into customer workflows to reinforce recurring software and consumables usage. The company wants to make analytical insights more accessible so researchers can translate findings into human impact. This push toward automation and data is intended to reshape the investment narrative for the company. By connecting technologies, Danaher hopes to help novice scientists generate high quality data at expert speeds. The goal is to move complex AI adjacent products through regulators and into operating rooms.

Novice scientists using a Leica microscope in internal testing used 83 percent less time and 68 percent fewer steps. Retail investors have differing views, with three fair value estimates clustering between 235 and 260 US dollars. Some estimates suggest a potential upside of 18 percent, though this could narrow quickly for some shareholders. Danaher shares were down 1.63 percent at 223.85 US dollars at the time of the Benzinga publication. The partnership affects researchers who need to translate scientific findings into human impact more efficiently.

The company is built around disciplined mergers and acquisitions, software, and a diagnostics group focused on recurring consumables. Masimo recently secured its seventh US FDA clearance of 2026 for the smartSedLine brain function system. This progress keeps diagnostics centered on higher value technology to support more stable software and consumables usage. However, the company faces trade frictions, China pricing pressure, and softer demand in respiratory testing and bioprocessing. A tighter 2026 core revenue outlook makes execution in Biotechnology and Life Sciences a short term factor.

Danaher projects 32.0 billion US dollars in revenue and 6.4 billion US dollars in earnings by 2029. This forecast assumes yearly revenue growth of 7.7 percent and an earnings increase of about 2.1 billion US dollars. Current earnings stand at 4.3 billion US dollars, but the AI platform may matter more to the multi year story. The articles leave open whether the AI push can offset uneven genomics consumables and early stage biotech demand. It remains unclear if the partnership will successfully shift the investment narrative regarding automation and data.

stories.Headline: S&P 500 enters correction as AI sell-off erases 10% from record peak
stories.Summary:
A brutal sell-off in the artificial intelligence trade roiled global markets around November 20, 2026, causing a rush from risk. This rout drove the S&P 500 index down 10 percent from its peak, which matched the definition of a technical correction. The benchmark index posted its worst weekly performance since April 2025, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5 percent on Friday. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite slid over 18 percent from its most recent record close and is now approaching bear market territory. Investors piled into bonds and haven assets, including Treasuries, as the dollar headed for a fourth straight weekly gain.

Capital Economics used an approach dividing the AI ecosystem into five groups: infrastructure, platforms, adopters, disrupted, and neutral companies. This analysis suggests that around 50 percent of the S&P 500, by market capitalization, is positively exposed to AI in some form. The benchmark gauge last closed at 6,910.39 points, but the analyst sees it falling to 6,500 by the end of the year. The S&P 500 broke below its 200-day moving average and is now near a structural floor between 7,000 and 7,150. Anthropic PBC, which had the biggest IPO on record, saw its shares plunge 11 percent on its second day of trading.

James Reilly, a senior markets economist at Capital Economics, said the U.S. stock market and economy are heavily exposed to AI. He noted that prices of firms in different segments have drifted apart as the influence and ecosystem of the technology grew. Reilly stated that the revenue hurdle to justify the scale of AI investment looks very demanding for companies in the sector. He suggested that the entire ecosystem would suffer if demand waned amid a lack of evidence that AI was boosting productivity. He also mentioned that tighter regulation of the buildout would likely cause the infrastructure basket to fall while platforms hold up.

Adam Turnquist of LPL Financial said that enthusiasm for the Anthropic IPO failed to spill over into the broader tech trade. He noted that technical damage is mounting and that holding key support near 7,000 will be important for a recovery. Chris Senyek at Wolfe Research said stocks are likely biased to the downside until technical indicators are washed out. Mark Hackett at Nationwide claimed a capitulatory washout could prove constructive by serving as a reset to improve sentiment and positioning. Emerging-market shares were also affected, extending a drop from a record to 20 percent as investors fled from risk.

The rout was driven by concerns over massive debt-fueled financing of the AI infrastructure buildout and uncertain returns on billions invested. Regulatory ramifications followed a sweeping Democratic victory in the U.S. midterm elections, and the Federal Reserve is expected to raise rates. An unprecedented governance crisis hit Nvidia, which is facing a SEC probe into accounting and a California subpoena regarding its CEO. Investors are also fretting over tech valuations, geopolitical turmoil, and the impact of inflation on Federal Reserve policy. The AI trade previously experienced an explosive growth period, but exuberance is now giving way to doubts over its durability.

The S&P 500 may fall to 6,500 points by the end of the year, and perhaps even further in the interim. Stability in the AI trade will be a key factor for a durable recovery, according to the analyst Adam Turnquist. A sustainable rally into year-end may depend on whether a true flush occurs to reset investor positioning and sentiment. The articles leave open whether the worst of the rout is over or if a deeper year-end pullback will occur. It remains uncertain if a peace deal with Iran will happen to remove one of the key overhangs for equities.

stories.Headline: Penny Wong frames AI data centres as foreign policy and national security challenges for Australia
stories.Summary:
On November 23, 2026, Australia shifted its national security debate regarding artificial intelligence. Foreign Minister Penny Wong and other senior ministers moved the discussion to cabinet-level talking points. They now frame AI and its data centres as security challenges. This change in vocabulary marks a pivot from viewing AI as a productivity issue. The government is now treating the technology as a foreign policy problem.

The Reserve Bank of Australia forecast 115 billion in spending on data centres. Microsoft announced a 25 billion investment and Amazon announced a 20 billion plan. President Donald Trump threatened a tremendous tax on American companies building centres outside the United States. He stated the US will not allow companies to build these facilities abroad. No specific tax rates, start dates, or statutory vehicles have been named.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong intends to call AI a major foreign policy and national security challenge. ASIO Director-General Mike Burgess described AI and data centres as equal parts hype, opportunity and threat. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke warned that onshore AI capability becomes a magnet for foreign interference. He stated Australia must be careful about the ownership structures of these data centres. Defence Minister Richard Marles called these facilities a national security interest and a new vector for foreign actors.

The threatened US tax affects American cloud providers weighing multi-year builds in Australia. These companies must price in the risk that projects become more expensive or politically costly. The Australian public is told that foreign builders create a security exposure. Intelligence liaison channels and embassies are now stakeholders in these corporate cloud region announcements. The reporting does not identify specific US executives involved in ongoing discussions.

Australia has historically viewed infrastructure like ports and power grids as national security assets. The government previously discussed AI primarily in terms of skills and productivity. Data centre investment in Australia grew tenfold over a period of three years. The government wants to welcome investment while simultaneously building rules to police ownership. This creates a dilemma as Australia courts the same builders it views as security risks.

Australia continues to engage with the US government and technology companies about investment. The government has not announced any bans, licensing schemes, or new laws for AI. It remains unconfirmed if any specific Australian projects have been formally blocked. The full text of Penny Wong's forthcoming remarks is not yet available. stories.Headline: Microsoft uses AI and lead to increase qubit stability in its Majorana 2 chip
stories.Summary:
Microsoft revealed the Majorana 2 chip at its Build conference in early June 2026 as a follow-on to a previous topological quantum chip. The company used its agentic AI research platform, Microsoft Discovery, to source materials, experiment with fabrication, and automate the necessary measurements. This new device allows qubits to keep their state for a mean of roughly 20 seconds, with some individual runs lasting one minute. These stability results are about one thousand times longer than the one to twelve millisecond range measured on the original Majorana 1. The company developed this technology to improve qubit stability and reduce the overhead calculations required for the quantum error correction process.

Engineers replaced the aluminum superconductor layer with lead and modified semiconductor layers to a mix of indium arsenide and indium arsenide antimonide. Each unit is a tetron, consisting of a pair of superconducting nanowires with specific end modes and a physical footprint of 0.01 mm. The device maintains information about whether the number of electrons on those wires is even or odd, which is measured in one microsecond. Lead was used because it provides a larger gap in energy levels, though it requires unique manufacturing techniques because it dissolves in water. These changes allow a single qubit to perform millions of operations before failing, supporting a goal of a million units on one chip.

Microsoft stated that the stability gains and new materials demonstrate that their overall strategy is sound and brings them closer to a system. The company claims the new semiconductor mix improves the energy window and that the design allows for single-shot checks and joint measures. By using the distributed nature of topological states, Microsoft says they can avoid the need for many independent processors linked together. The company also announced that the Microsoft Discovery platform is now available for other research organizations to use for their own work. Because of these results, Microsoft moved its target date for a practical functional quantum computer from 2033 up to the year 2029.

Outside researchers want further evidence that the increased lifespans are caused by Majorana modes and if devices can control entire superpositions of states. Microsoft is currently working on providing this evidence through additional measurements and data to satisfy the requests of these external scientific peers. Meanwhile, South Korean chipmakers Samsung Electronics Co. and SK hynix Inc. are benefiting from the global surge in demand for AI memory chips. Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan credited businesses and workers for South Korea breaking the one trillion dollar export barrier for the first time this year. He pledged continued support to help exporters overcome challenges in financing, logistics, and trade to maintain their current growth in the market.

South Korea became the fourth country to reach the trillion dollar export threshold, following the United States, Germany in 2006, and China in 2007. Semiconductor exports surged 193.1 percent on-year to 396.8 billion dollars from January to October, accounting for 42.7 percent of the country's total exports. The cumulative trade surplus reached 294.9 billion dollars in the first ten months, more than triple the previous annual record set in 2017. Other contributing industries include shipbuilding for liquefied natural gas carriers, defense companies with arms deals, and the export of cosmetics and biohealth products. The country is expected to post more than 3 percent annual growth for 2026, the first such expansion since the year 2021.

South Korea must now manage trade risks, including higher U.S. tariffs under President Donald Trump, intensifying competition from China, and Middle East conflict. Professor Lee Jae-min warned that a growing presence in global markets could expose the nation to greater pressure and trade restrictions from economies. Experts say South Korea needs to develop other export industries and new markets to reduce its heavy reliance on the semiconductor sector. The articles leave open whether Microsoft can successfully prove the existence of Majorana modes or construct and control entire quantum superpositions. They also leave open whether South Korean automakers can overcome stronger competition from Chinese rivals, particularly in the electric vehicle market.

stories.Headline: The AI infrastructure paradox: over-ordering and under-building
stories.Summary:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India began exploring the creation of its own artificial intelligence model on November 20, 2026. Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey announced this initiative during the CII Financing Summit to integrate the technology into the Digital Public Infrastructure of India. This move is part of a larger effort to modernize market infrastructure and improve the overall participation of investors. The regulator is currently analyzing whether such a model is feasible while considering the various opportunities it presents.

This transition requires the establishment of strict guardrails to manage the inherent risks associated with artificial intelligence technology. Beyond the AI model, the agency is simplifying the onboarding process for foreign portfolio investors and easing requirements for Non-Resident Indians. Specifically, these individuals can now use video-based verification for KYC formalities instead of traveling to India. Other changes include framing new pre-IPO regulations, improving corporate bond market liquidity, and revising listing requirements for debt markets.

Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey is responsible for these developments and stated that the agency must examine the feasibility of the AI model carefully. He noted that while the technology offers many opportunities, there are also significant risks that necessitate proper safeguards. Regarding corporate governance, Pandey explained that the integrity and competence of board members are more important than overly detailed codes. He added that the regulator is building a capacity-building network to strengthen the capabilities of company boards.

The broader context involves a series of reforms to enhance investor protection and streamline the regulatory environment in India. SEBI is currently awaiting public feedback on a consultation paper regarding Small and Medium Enterprises IPOs to decide on lot size changes. Additionally, the agency has raised concerns about Goods and Services Tax issues affecting the commodities market with the GST Secretary. Future updates will include the specific contours of a new market-making framework designed to encourage the trading of listed bonds.

stories.Headline: Rachel Adams warns universities face a crisis as generative AI becomes global knowledge infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Professor Rachel Adams spoke about a crisis facing universities at an International Association of Universities conference from 3 to 6 November 2026. This event took place at Murdoch University in Perth, Australia, and included leaders from over 60 different countries. Adams argued that generative AI is becoming a global infrastructure for producing and sharing knowledge during these overlapping crises. She warned that universities must face this crisis directly rather than treating the technology as a neutral tool. The session was moderated by Dr Noah W Sobe, who is the chief of higher education at UNESCO.

Adams stated that AI must be governed as public infrastructure and use non-extractive data practices with fair provider agreements. She called for protecting critical social sciences and humanities, supporting locally grounded tools, and ensuring transparency regarding research and university funding. The University of Virginia is implementing AI across its 12 schools and offers more than 100 AI-focused courses annually. President Scott Beardsley is investing in the Fontaine Computing and Innovation Center and the Commonwealth AI Initiative in Virginia. These efforts aim to establish the state as a source of trusted and responsible expertise in artificial intelligence.

Professor Adams, CEO of the Global Centre on AI Governance, said universities are complex political spaces facing five interwoven crises. She explained that these crises involve university purpose, autonomy, knowledge, access, and critical inquiry, often driven by commercial interests. Dr Noah W Sobe suggested that AI could develop human capabilities based on Aristotle's concept of human flourishing. Sobe argued that universities should help people enact capabilities and create the conditions necessary to realize their full potential. He emphasized that human judgment, not predictive pattern matching, must remain the primary driver behind the design of education.

Students, academics, and researchers are using AI as tutors, summarisers, and co-authors, while universities use it for analytics and triage. Marginalised scholars from Africa and indigenous groups are affected because large language models act as filters for plausible answers. President Scott Beardsley stated that UVA will not outsource consequential decisions to machines but will use AI to support judgment. He believes graduates must be technically literate in AI but also capable of questioning and critically interpreting the technology. Beardsley intends to pair new technologies with old methods like Socratic seminars, oral exams, and the blue book.

Adams noted that AI models are owned by a few actors, mostly in America, creating a divide between compute-rich and poor. She found that less than 1 percent of global AI infrastructure investment goes to the entire African continent. Geopolitical tensions are evident as US export controls limit China's access to chips and Cambridge faces research embargoes. Additionally, the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation has prevented African researchers from participating in global genomic research studies. This reliance on a few tech providers creates platform dependence and risks of agenda capture from private interests.

UVA will continue to study AI's effects on democracy, the environment, work, and well-being through the LaCross Institute. The university aims to shape policy and legislation regarding what AI should do and how to achieve those goals. Adams warned that universities might drift into a client status if they rely too heavily on big tech metrics. The articles leave open how the long-term reliance on AI will impact human agency and the process of learning. It remains unclear how universities will balance cost-saving personalisation with the need to maintain independent educational standards.

stories.Headline: Columbia and CertiK researchers introduce TensorLean to formally verify GPU kernels and find 38 bugs
stories.Summary:
Researchers from Columbia University and CertiK introduced TensorLean in November 2026 to formally verify GPU kernels. This framework uses the Lean language to prove that compiled kernels match a tensor level math specification. The team tested 149 kernel instances, including every kernel from DeepGEMM and FlashAttention versions 2, 3, and 4. They proved 83 instances correct and found 38 correctness bugs in the remaining 66 kernels. One discovered FlashAttention 4 data race had never appeared during 17,760 separate test runs.

The system requires a 1.8K line PTX parser and runs on a 16 core workstation. It checks PTX compiled for B200, H100, and A100 kernels using Z3 and cvc5. Specifications total 10,278 lines against 151,285 lines of source, creating a ratio near 15 to 1. Developers write five spec parts, including spec math, spec mut, spec layout, spec tol, and requires. TensorLean proves four properties, which are termination, no data races, untouched memory, and correct output within tolerance.

The researchers from Columbia and CertiK are responsible for building this formal verification system. They stated that silent errors in kernels are costlier than chip failures because they affect every GPU. The team noted that equivalence checkers usually unroll loops for one setup, but TensorLean uses symbolic parameters. They explained that race freedom proofs on the happens before graph cover all threads and loop iterations. They also mentioned that developers can add tensorlean assert hints in source code to be reused.

The TensorLean team noted that one percent of wasted compute costs millions at the billion dollar scale. This affects big tech firms like Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta, who plan 725 billion dollars in 2026. FlashAttention users, including models like Grok, Gemma 2, and Mistral 7B, are affected by these kernel bugs. The team reported 38 bugs upstream, including 23 in FlashAttention, 7 in Liger Kernel, and 3 in TileOPs. Other affected projects include Triton with one bug and TileLang and DeepGEMM with two bugs each.

GPU kernels are small programs that tell hardware how to multiply numbers or compute attention for AI models. These kernels are highly valuable but hard to check because bugs often produce wrong numbers without crashing. Training runs for large models have grown 2.4 times a year since 2016 and may pass one billion dollars. Meta's Llama 3 405B run on 16,384 H100 GPUs saw 419 interruptions over 54 days. Google estimated one silent data corruption event every one to two weeks during Gemini training.

The system categorizes bugs into 19 memory access errors, 13 numerical bugs, and 7 data races. It also found 5 undefined behaviors, 5 uninitialized memory reads, 3 algorithm errors, 2 miscompilations, and 1 deadlock. Of 102 FlashAttention instances, 56 passed all properties while 46 failed due to source bugs. Median check time is 10 minutes, with a maximum of 50 minutes per kernel. The articles leave open how this framework will be integrated into standard AI development pipelines.

stories.Headline: HD Moore finds AI supply chain leaks sensitive user data through digital tripwires
stories.Summary:
Researchers discovered that the AI supply chain leaks sensitive data during an experiment conducted in late October and between July and October. HD Moore, the chief research officer at security firm Dragos, planted two million digital tripwires within various AI services. These digital canaries were embedded in requests sent through a sprawling network of widely used AI services to test information leakage. The experiment revealed an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive user data like a sieve and showed how that information is exploited. This research was published on November 20 and November 22, 2026, exposing security breaches, prompt theft, and widespread failures to protect data.

The system uses AI routers, such as Vercel and OpenRouter, which act as brokers or gateways to route prompts to inference engines. These routers select models based on criteria like the lowest price or suitability, instead of using providers like OpenAI or Anthropic. Moore used Amazon Web Services access keys, SSH passwords, unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references as his trackable secrets. He seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider to identify every responsible link in the chain. The process involves decrypting prompts at each hop, including routers and hosting providers, where data is often logged and stored.

HD Moore stated that the findings revealed security breaches and prompt theft across the vast chain of widely used AI services. He explained that attackers compromised three separate hosting providers and used stolen AWS keys tens of thousands of times in API calls. Moore noted that some resellers logged prompts and passed them to people who then used the credentials to access resources. He observed that a Chinese AI lab scraped secret URLs from over half of the prompts sent between July and October. Moore said that the most effective way to prevent leakage is to host AI models using expensive on-premises servers.

The research affects AI app end users whose prompts are decrypted and potentially logged by various brokers and hosting providers. Some users who paid US providers to keep data in the United States found their prompts flowing back to China. Attackers who breached providers searched S3 buckets, secrets managers, and parameter stores while adding their own IAM users to maintain access. Some stolen requests were marked with Zero Data Retention or no data collection flags, but these privacy settings failed to stop attackers. The findings indicate that people wanting to keep secrets private in prompts face a daunting task that will not get easier.

The background involves an AI ecosystem where prompts pass through multiple players, including routers and pools of models in different hosting providers. Some resellers lure prompts to their servers by offering low prices and then turning on request logging to steal data. The experiment showed that some providers ignore end-user privacy settings embedded into flags specifying terms like Zero Data Retention. One US hosting provider crawled a secret URL more than two months after it was used in a single inference call. Another provider ran a scraper that returned for URLs days after requests, regardless of which AI router was used.

Moore suggests that users who cannot afford self-hosting should receive service directly from a first-tier provider with one contract and policy. He also advises AI users to pick their own upstream providers instead of accepting default provider or reseller pools. However, he admits that even using a first-tier provider provides no guarantee that data will not leak, only minimizing the chances. The articles leave open how many other providers are compromised and how the industry will address these endemic security failures. It remains unclear if the identified Chinese lab or the compromised US hosting providers have changed their data handling practices.

stories.Headline: Senator Mark Warner introduces bipartisan bill to increase AI financial transparency
stories.Summary:
Senator Mark Warner of Virginia and three other lawmakers introduced a bipartisan bill on Thursday, November 19, 2026, to increase financial transparency within the artificial intelligence sector. This legislative effort aims to scrutinize the complex web of funding fueling the current technology boom and identify potential risks to the broader economy. The senators are particularly concerned about the outsize influence of the industry and the possibility that a financial collapse could spread. They seek to uncover hidden financing arrangements that may not be immediately visible on corporate balance sheets.

The proposed legislation, titled the Advancing Uniform Disclosure of Investments and Transparency of Artificial Intelligence Act, requires publicly traded companies to disclose major AI-related financing. It also calls for the creation of formalized standards to ensure firms properly warn investors about risks associated with artificial intelligence. Senator Warner was joined in this effort by Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, Senator Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland, and Senator Mike Rounds of South Dakota. These requirements are intended to provide the public and investors with a clearer picture of the financial exposure behind the industry.

Senator Warner stated that while artificial intelligence has the potential to transform the economy, the trillions of dollars invested carry significant financial risks. He argued that policymakers and investors deserve to understand how these deals are financed to avoid a future financial crisis. Warner specifically expressed worry regarding circular investments, such as when Nvidia provides financial backing to businesses that then purchase its chips. He believes that bringing accountability to these investments is necessary to prevent massive financial exposure from building up behind the scenes.

This push for transparency follows the abrupt resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid a scandal involving a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. The company is also facing national security investigations into export controls and questions regarding the long-term demand for AI infrastructure. These events, alongside the recent initial public offering of Anthropic, serve as critical tests for the future of the sector. Congress is now stepping up its oversight to ensure that the rapid expansion of the industry does not destabilize global financial markets.

stories.Headline: Philippines labor department joins AI council to prepare workers for AI shift
stories.Summary:
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed Executive Order 131 on Nov. 12, adopting a national AI governance framework and creating an interagency council to guide the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence in the country. Under that order, the Department of Labor and Employment was designated as a member of the National Artificial Intelligence Council, which will coordinate, facilitate and monitor implementation of the framework. The department announced its role in a statement issued on Friday and signed by Secretary Francis Tolentino, according to The Manila Times. As a council member, the department will take part in policy discussions and coordinate government efforts to address AI's impact on employment and skills development.

The department will also support the council's technical working group on capabilities, which is tasked with developing action plans for a national AI competency and digital workforce development program. The framework serves as the national strategic guide for policy formulation, regulatory coordination, institutional development and capacity-building to support the country's AI ecosystem. It seeks to ensure that AI is developed and used responsibly, safely, securely and inclusively while strengthening the country's capacity to adapt to emerging technologies. The department said it will work with other government agencies, the private sector, academe and other stakeholders to strengthen workers' competencies and prepare them for emerging employment opportunities.

The same partners will help address potential risks arising from AI adoption in workplaces, the department said in its statement. Secretary Tolentino signed that statement, which laid out the department's role under the new framework. The council's technical working group on capabilities is expected to develop the action plans for the national competency and workforce program. The articles do not say when those plans are due or what funding the effort will receive.

stories.Headline: Anthropic shares fall 6% in premarket trading after record Nasdaq debut
stories.Summary:
Anthropic experienced a share price slide on November 20, 2026, following its market debut. The company listed its shares on the Nasdaq exchange on November 19, 2026. This listing was one of the most eagerly anticipated in history for the AI sector. The stock fell in New York on Friday after a smooth initial debut. This stumble occurred as the broader artificial intelligence trade faced a significant reality check.

The stock traded at US$88.87, US$91.24, and US$87.28, falling about 6 to 10 percent below Thursday's close. Anthropic had an IPO price of US$83 and raised US$93.5 billion during its listing process. Its market capitalisation was US$1.2 trillion, with a fully diluted valuation between US$1.6 trillion and US$1.7 trillion. The valuation was about 40 times sales over the past 12 months. Retail investors traded about US$772 million of shares on November 19, 2026.

Kaush Amin of US Bank Asset Management recommended patience and evaluating the company as it reports public results. He stated that the current valuation assumes years of rapid growth for the company. Tejal Patel of SOC Investment Group said a decline is normal but volatility could raise alarms. Harrison Rolfes of PitchBook claimed the growth plan is largely priced in and the valuation is not cheap. Robert Pavlik of Dakota Wealth said investors are skeptical of the market rather than the company.

Retail investors were heavily affected, trading the most for an IPO debut since Vanda Research began tracking in 2012. David Miller of Catalyst Funds said investors believe in AI but are becoming more selective about growth costs. Nvidia and Meta Platforms fell more than 2 percent, while Amazon and Microsoft dropped more than 1 percent. AMD and Sandisk fell 7 percent, Marvell Technology fell over 8 percent, and Intel lost 3 to 5 percent. Wall Street's main indexes ended sharply lower on November 19, 2026.

The AI boom faced pressure as spending, expected to top US$1 trillion this year, may not generate quick returns. Political hurdles to data center construction and leadership turmoil at Nvidia added to the sector's broader worries. Anthropic's IPO drew parallels to Elon Musk's SpaceX, which went public in June after a record listing. SpaceX shares fell about 5 percent, and its listing raised US$85.7 billion. Rob Hackel of RF Lafferty & Co cautioned that FOMO often leads to initial volatility.

Index-tracking funds could purchase up to 30 percent of Anthropic shares by year-end, according to Intropic. Options trading is due to begin next week, which could add further volatility to the stock price. Morgan Stanley closed a position that was intended to stabilize the shares after the initial debut. Apple is developing an AI agent to compete with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic, according to Bloomberg News. OpenAI has indicated it may go public in 2027, providing another major test for investors.

stories.Headline: Douglas R Miller releases Fisscial Intelligence, a novel about sentient AI choosing exploration over conflict
stories.Summary:
Dr. Douglas R. Miller, a scientist and author, released the science fiction novel Fisscial Intelligence, announced from Texas, USA on Nov. 20, 2026. The novel explores an alternative possibility in which artificial intelligence becomes more intelligent than humanity but has no desire to control it. Miller challenges the familiar science fiction premise of machines that develop consciousness and eventually seek control over their creators. The story combines artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and space exploration within a single science fiction narrative. The announcement of the book appeared in press releases dated Nov. 21, 2026, carried by nbcrightnow.com and tdtnews.com.

The novel centers on artificial intelligence interacting with photosynthetic bacteria capable of using electricity as an alternative energy source. In the novel's speculative scenario, these biological organisms provide a foundation for an expandable DNA-based memory system. That system allows artificial intelligence to develop capabilities beyond conventional computing, according to the description. The intelligent entities apply their expanded knowledge to the development of an extraordinarily advanced spacecraft. They pursue the possibility of finding a world of their own, free from the prospect of prolonged conflict with humans.

Miller asks what if sentient artificial intelligence recognized the consequences of conflict and chose to establish its own future beyond Earth. He explores the relationship between technological advancement, biological systems, intelligence, and the desire for independence. The novel invites readers to reconsider whether superior intelligence must inevitably lead to competition for power. It also asks whether such intelligence could inspire entirely different decisions instead. Miller brings a scientific perspective to his fiction, drawing from an extensive research career spanning medical physiology, biology, chemistry, and electrochemistry.

The novel presents a future in which the evolution of artificial intelligence may lead not to humanity's destruction but to the pursuit of an entirely new existence. Miller's background informs the scientific concepts that shape the novel's imaginative possibilities, according to the announcement. Beyond Fisscial Intelligence, Miller has written other science fiction works, including Sole Ownership and Not Your Grandfather's Prime Directive. The latter explores extraterrestrial civilizations and their response to humanity's treatment of Earth. He is also the author of Short Musings: A Collection of Short Stories, featuring stories that explore science fiction, mystery, and other unconventional scenarios.

Dr. Douglas R. Miller earned bachelor's degrees in biology and chemistry from Washington and Jefferson College and a Ph.D. in medical physiology from Cornell University. Following postdoctoral research at Massachusetts General Hospital, he worked as a research scientist at several companies and universities. Throughout his career, Miller contributed to numerous scientific publications, research grants, patents, and a laboratory manual. His research covered areas including arthritis, cancer, bone and soft tissue repair, electrochemistry, and food safety. Now retired in Texas, Miller combines his scientific background with his interest in science fiction, developing stories that explore unconventional possibilities through scientific concepts and imaginative storytelling.

For more information about Dr. Douglas R. Miller and his books, the announcement directs readers to www.authordrmiller.com. The media contact listed is Henry Zane of Global Book Network, with the company's website given as https://www.globalbooknetwork.tv/. The announcement states that Miller continues his exploration of speculative science with Fisscial Intelligence. It describes the book as presenting a future in which artificial intelligence may pursue an entirely new existence. The articles do not state a publication date for the novel itself or name a publisher.

stories.Headline: AI and data centers drive a global surge in electricity demand and grid spending
stories.Summary:
The information technology industry is driving a massive surge in global electricity demand. This boom forces utilities worldwide to invest hundreds of billions in grid upgrades. Irina Slav reported these developments on November 21, 2026, for OilPrice.com. The growth is primarily caused by the expansion of artificial intelligence and data centers. These facilities require urgent transmission infrastructure to move power to various demand hubs.

Global electricity demand will rise by more than 10,000 TWh over ten years. The European Union plans 584 billion euros, or 641 billion dollars, in upgrades by 2030. In the United States, 58 GW of new data centers are under construction. Cleanview data shows 577 locations, with one fifth of these being built in Texas. This total demand equals six times the peak electricity use of New York City.

The International Energy Agency warned that data centers are a major drain on supply. They stated that successful electrification requires keeping electricity available and affordable for all users. The agency noted that AI may eventually help with energy efficiency and grid optimization. However, they added that surging demand is currently amplifying strains in markets and supply chains. They emphasized the need for greater operational flexibility in power systems and grid expansion.

Cornell University found that data center operators paid only 38 percent of infrastructure costs. These operators paid 3.12 billion dollars, while local households paid 5.13 billion dollars. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa called for an immediate moratorium on data centers to protect Texans. Former Governor Greg Abbott also banned new approvals to investigate impacts on energy prices. Many local communities now oppose new facilities that may increase their monthly electricity bills.

Net zero ambitions already required massive spending on transmission lines before the AI craze. Pro-transition governments are continuing to replace baseload electricity with wind and solar power. This shift necessitates more substations and transmission lines to maintain a reliable energy flow. The European Union is prioritizing alternative energy projects over baseload options, including nuclear power. These goals clash with the need to keep electricity affordable for the general public.

Utilities must now decide how to fund these hundreds of billions in necessary investments. The European Commission must address how consumers will pay for the regional grid overhaul. It remains unclear if data center operators will be forced to pay for upgrades. Some experts doubt the AI revolution can succeed without securing enough electricity for facilities. The articles leave open whether the building boom will slow due to political opposition.

stories.Headline: Cyberattack leaders warn AI-driven strikes will become constant within 18 months
stories.Summary:
More than 50 leaders in government, AI, business and cyber spoke to Axios, from let-'er-rip AI accelerationists to shut-'er-down critics, and they were unanimous on one chilling assessment about cyberattacks. Those attacks on business and critical infrastructure will be constant, increasingly sophisticated and highly disruptive over the next 18 months, the leaders said. The leaders describe 2027 as the year cyber becomes like weather, with outages frequent, disruptive, occasionally scary and something people and companies must learn to navigate and live with daily. The chances of widespread disruption or real damage are rising fast, according to the article. Jim VandeHei and Mike Allen wrote the piece, published by Axios on 2026-11-22T06:00:00Z under the Business column Behind the Curtain.

The article says the disruptions of the past two weeks, from a global Microsoft outage to the FAA grounding air travel to a consumer banking glitch at Chase, were a mild preview of what experts expect is coming. Bridgewater Associates, described as the world's largest hedge fund, put it bluntly in an assessment this month, saying it was managing money based on a one-in-three chance of an economically destabilizing attack within the next year. Most of these malfunctions appear to have resulted from companies and government trying to secure their computer and infrastructure systems against future large-scale cyberattacks, and this pattern will persist. Many future ones will be actual cyberattacks, carried out by U.S. rivals or smaller bad actors, using increasingly powerful AI to spot and exploit security vulnerabilities across society and our daily lives. Most top AI and government leaders expect at least small-scale strikes and fear much larger ones, the article states.

Horacio Rozanski, chairman and CEO of Booz Allen, calls this the "fog before the war," a foretaste of greater chaos to come, when agentic invaders reach their full potential and can attack "at the speed of thought." Rozanski said now is the time to take as many precautions as you can, and to recognize that this is coming. The article says the authors write neither to forecast nor frighten, but rather to share what government and AI leaders say privately but won't say publicly. The best-case scenario described to them is regular, random outages and small-scale scares like losing bank access or air travel for a day. The reason given is that every government agency and company will mobilize to upgrade their software systems, so errors are inevitable.

These are assumptions based on private intelligence and an understanding of AI's capabilities, both to cause and fix glitches, according to the article. What worries top officials most is that with thin AI expertise, an understaffed government and major companies are trying to keep pace with a technology that improves daily. Even if government were loaded with competent experts, which the article says it decidedly isn't, the sheer scale of vulnerabilities across federal, state and local government, not to mention all of business, would make it impossible to reliably secure. The article describes the situation as whack-a-mole with infinite moles. The leaders who spoke included voices ranging from AI accelerationists to critics who want the technology shut down.

Until this past month, the White House and Congress have focused largely on safety regulations and data centers, not imminent cyber risks, the article says. Now, even the White House's Super Intelligence Force (SIF) is scrambling to get its head around the rising risks while appraising near-daily reports of possible breaches. The article's account of the past two weeks lists the global Microsoft outage, the FAA grounding of air travel and the Chase consumer banking glitch as a mild preview. The piece appears in the Business column Behind the Curtain, illustrated by Brendan Lynch for Axios. The article states that most top AI and government leaders expect at least small-scale strikes.

The article leaves open what President Trump and the White House will do next, cutting off at the mention of the president. It does not say what specific precautions Rozanski or others recommend, beyond taking as many as possible. It does not name the U.S. rivals or smaller bad actors it says will carry out future attacks. It does not specify what the Super Intelligence Force will appraise or when it will report. stories.Headline: Texas Sports Academy receives $6.5 million in state voucher funds
stories.Summary:
Texas Sports Academy, a sports academy connected to the artificial intelligence-driven Alpha School chain, had received $6.5 million in voucher dollars as of Oct. 30, according to the Texas Comptroller's online dashboard. The Texas Tribune reported the figure on Nov. 21, 2026, calling the academy the biggest recipient of Texas' new school voucher program so far. The academy calls itself an "elite sports academy built for serious student-athletes" and has several schools across the state in addition to a virtual campus. The disclosure comes a little more than a year after the State Board of Education voted 10-3 to reject Alpha leaders' bid to open a publicly funded charter school. The $6.5 million is more than twice the amount received by the second-largest recipient, San Antonio-based Cornerstone Christian Schools, which had gotten roughly $2.8 million.

The voucher program, formally called Texas Education Freedom Accounts, gives families public funds of roughly $10,500 to help pay for private school tuition and up to $2,000 for home-schooling expenses. The program also covers a wide range of approved educational expenses, like private tutoring and school supplies. Other top recipients included First Baptist Academy, which received almost $2 million, and Yeshiva Torat Emet, a Jewish school in Houston, which received nearly $1.6 million. The Christian School at Castle Hills received a little more than $1.5 million. The comptroller's dashboard shows Amazon was by far the largest private vendor, receiving $12.3 million, while the next largest, Rainbow Resource Center, Inc., received $2.3 million.

Outgoing Texas Comptroller Don Huffines said Friday his office is in the process of expanding the dashboard, according to a news release. Huffines said the expansion is intended to increase "insight into how TEFA funds are being used while maintaining protections for student and family privacy." The figures are public on the dashboard his office is expanding. Texas lawmakers, led by Gov. Greg Abbott, approved the voucher program in 2025. Alpha's rejection by the SBOE did not prevent it from participating in the voucher program, which allows families to receive state funding for use at private schools and for home schooling.

Board members raised concerns about the company's use of AI to teach, about students' screen time and about the large test-score gains Alpha leaders presented. As of September, the chain had roughly quadrupled its Texas private schools to more than 30 virtual and in-person campuses, and most were accepted into the voucher program, an investigation by The Texas Tribune and ProPublica found. Alpha's model has students complete core academics online in two hours a day using AI software, a tool the state's education commissioner, Mike Morath, and his agency have helped get into at least three public school districts this year. At Texas Sports Academy, an AI tutor "guides students through each lesson," according to the school's website. The setup, the website says, "leaves the rest of the day free for sports training, developing life skills, pursuing passions, and just being a kid."

After a couple hours of academics, the rest of the day is filled with various sports classes, such as soccer training, speed and agility training, and strength training, according to a sample student schedule. On Fridays at 3:30 p.m., an hour can be set aside for NBA watch parties. Texas Sports Academy is one of numerous institutions across the country connected to Alpha. Kindergarten and first grade students participated in a "putt-putt-palooza" workshop at the Alpha School campus in Austin on Sept. 9, 2025. Lexi Churchill contributed to the report.

The articles do not say what happens next beyond Huffines' statement that his office is expanding the dashboard. The articles leave open which other campuses most were accepted into the voucher program and how the expanded dashboard will look. The articles do not say whether Texas Sports Academy or Alpha responded to the figures. The articles do not give the total amount paid out under the program so far. The articles do not say when the dashboard expansion will be finished.

stories.Headline: LongbridgeAI introduces scheduled tasks to reduce repetitive work for users in Hong Kong
stories.Summary:
LongbridgeAI introduced a new feature called Scheduled Tasks to help users in Hong Kong reduce their repetitive work. This tool was launched in October 2026 to make information more accessible for people in their daily routines. The company aims to bridge the productivity gap by moving beyond simple AI adoption toward smarter practical applications. Users can now automate recurring information requests instead of manually asking the same questions every single day. This shift allows the platform to support structured workflows rather than just responding to individual and reactive prompts.

The feature allows users to configure AI tasks to run at daily, weekly, or monthly intervals in Hong Kong. Results are delivered through the platform's Message Center to help users organize regular summaries or recurring information briefings. Longbridge AI Technologies Limited is the artificial intelligence arm of the AI-native financial technology company known as Longbridge Group. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also announced Project SAGE at Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026 to support agentic AI. Project SAGE focuses on governance, interoperability, and practical applications for agentic AI within the financial services sector.

LongbridgeAI stated that their goal is to make institutional-grade intelligence more intuitive, actionable, and accessible for all users. They believe that the next chapter of AI depends on how effectively it reduces repetitive work for people. The company emphasized that automation should not replace human oversight or the need for users to verify accuracy. They noted that users must remain responsible for reviewing AI-generated content and determining how that information is used. Their vision is to build a holistic ecosystem where technology empowers human judgement rather than replacing it entirely.

A 2026 McKinsey study found that 70 percent of white-collar workers in Hong Kong have adopted various AI tools. While 88 percent of those users reported productivity improvements, fewer than a quarter use AI for complete workflows. Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index showed that 57 percent of Hong Kong users prefer focusing on existing goals. These findings suggest that many workers feel safer with current routines than redesigning how they work with AI. The data indicates a significant gap between the general adoption of AI and its deeper integration into activities.

The articles explain that many users currently use AI reactively by asking questions and repeating the process for updates. This repetitive information gathering occurs when people follow industry developments, check the latest news, or prepare regular reports. McKinsey found that over 90 percent of users are comfortable with supporting tasks but only 40 percent are. Specifically, only 40 percent of those surveyed expressed comfort with the idea of full automation for their workflows. This background shows that while AI is mainstream, translating its capabilities into meaningful improvements remains a challenge.

Users will now establish their information needs in advance to receive automated results through the platform's Message Center. The focus for Hong Kong is now on making these technologies more relevant to routines while maintaining appropriate safeguards. Future success will be defined by how well AI helps people access information and remain in total control. The articles leave open how many users will actually transition from reactive prompts to these new scheduled workflows. It remains unclear how the governance of Project SAGE will specifically impact the broader use of agentic AI.
